pool.name: Let winners run: exit at the close or with a trailing stop instead of a fixed R target (Zarattini & Aziz ORB exit grid, plus the noise-area paper's VWAP trailing stop)
pool.published_rules: Zarattini & Aziz 2023 (SSRN 4416622), 5-minute ORB on QQQ/TQQQ. The base case puts the stop at the low (or high) of the first 5-minute candle with a 10R target or an end-of-day exit, whichever comes first. The sensitivity grid then puts the stop at a fraction of the 14-day ATR and tries targets from 1R to 10R plus end-of-day: 'the best results were achieved ... with tight stop losses (5% of the 14-day ATR) and by keeping the trade active until EoD'. Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz 2024 exit only at the stop or at 16:00, and cite Wu et al. (Taiwan index futures, genetic-algorithm ORB): 'the introduction of a profit target is detrimental', while a stop loss improves results. Noise-area paper (SFI RP 24-97): the trailing stop for a long is max(current upper band, VWAP) and for a short min(current lower band, VWAP). It is checked only at HH:00 and HH:30, and everything is flat at the close.
pool.published_params: Stop at 5-10 % of the 14-day ATR in the US papers (NOT portable to NSE futures, see risks). Target grid 1R-10R vs end-of-day, with end-of-day best. Trailing stop = VWAP or the current noise band, checked every 30 minutes.
pool.claimed_performance: QQQ ORB 2016-2023 (in sample): TQQQ +1,484 % vs passive QQQ +169 %, with the heat map of average R best at a 5 % ATR stop and end-of-day exit. Noise-area SPY 2007-2024 (in sample, net of $0.0035/share commission): moving from an opposite-band stop to a current band + VWAP trail took Sharpe from 0.61 to 1.24, MDD from 21 % to 12 %, worst day from -10.3 % to -4.8 % and skew from -1.24 to +1.29. Hit ratio fell from 54 % to 43 %. Trades rose from 5,494 to 7,668, with average PnL $0.10 to $0.09 per share. A VWAP-only trail did worse (Sharpe 1.17 vs 1.35, dynamic sizing). None of these numbers is out of sample, and all are on US ETFs.
pool.our_data_mapping: Pure harness test for three of the four declared settings, chosen on the design window: (a) ('s_fable_op', 75, 'CLOSE_TR', 6); (b) ('s_fable_op', 75, 'CLOSE', 6); (c) ('s_fable_op', 75, 'T3_TR', 6); the same three on 's_opus_v3' for reference. Columns net_CLOSE / net_CLOSE_TR / net_T3_TR are 100 % populated in real, unseen and known. Setting (d) is a VWAP trail and needs a minute re-sim on cash candles from H.minute_data(). It keeps the scanner's structural stop and entry at the next minute's open. At each 30-minute mark from the open (09:45, 10:15 ... 15:15 IST), a long exits at that minute's close if close < session VWAP (a short if close > VWAP), and anything left is squared off at 15:29. Price it with scanner.equity.fills plus lots_for/round_trip/slippage(0.02). Setting (d) runs cleanly only on unseen/known; on real it could only be approximated with the cash path.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial. T3 is already Fable-OP's baseline exit. 'Stop to breakeven after 0.4-0.8R' was tried, and the *_TR columns move the stop to entry after 1R, which is similar. However, the brief says T2_TR/T3_TR/CLOSE_TR/CLOSE were never compared systematically against the baselines. The VWAP trail is new.
pool.why_it_could_beat: Every ORB/intraday-momentum paper finds the payoff right-skewed: a few trend days pay for many small losses, so capping winners at 1R throws away the tail. The data already agree, since Fable-OP at T3 beats Opus at T1 on real and unseen. CLOSE_TR keeps the tail but gives back less on days that reverse after 1R. That should help max DD and worst day, which is where Fable-OP is weakest (worst day -56,275).
pool.risks: The US papers' tight-stop half does not transfer. Futures costs in costs.py (STT 0.05 % sell side, about 0.096 % of notional per round trip including 0.02 %/side slippage) are about 0.3R a trade at a 0.1-ATR stop, against about 0.14R at 0.3 ATR, so keep the scanner's stop. Holding to the close exposes shorts to end-of-day loser rebounds (candidate 7). The VWAP trail is checked on cash, not futures. Returns are path-dependent, and choosing among 4 exits on one window still selects.

pool.name: Noise-area filter: require the signal to be outside the stock's own time-of-day 'noise band' (Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon, Beat the Market)
pool.published_rules: For day t and each time of day HH:MM: move_{t-i,HH:MM} = |Close_{t-i,HH:MM}/Open_{t-i,9:30} - 1| for i = 1..14, and sigma_{t,HH:MM} = the mean of those 14 values. UpperBound = max(Open_t, Close_{t-1}) x (1 + VM x sigma) and LowerBound = min(Open_t, Close_{t-1}) x (1 - VM x sigma); the gap adjustment widens the band on the side opposite the gap. Above UpperBound means abnormal buying (go long), below LowerBound means abnormal selling (go short). Decisions are taken only at HH:00/HH:30 'to mitigate the risk of overtrading caused by short-term market fluctuations'.
pool.published_params: Lookback 14 days (paper); lookback insensitive (5 to 90 days give Sharpe 1.23-1.50, best at 90). Volatility multiplier VM = 1 (paper); best risk-adjusted VM is about 1.5; higher VM gives fewer trades and lower total return. Checks every 30 minutes.
pool.claimed_performance: SPY May 2007-2024 net of commissions: unlevered (current band + VWAP stop) 380 % total, IRR 9.7 %, vol 7.7 %, Sharpe 1.24, MDD 12 %. Vol-targeted (2 % daily target, max 4x): 1,985 %, IRR 19.6 %, Sharpe 1.33, MDD 25 %. 7,668 trades, 37 % hit. The authors' FAQ applies the same rules to 33 futures 2007-2024: 31 of 33 positive, average Sharpe 0.60, portfolio Sharpe 1.65. Their liquid-stock and ETF basket 2018-Aug 2024 is described only as 'Sharpe exceeds 2' (authors' own, no table). Not peer reviewed, no held-out period. Parameter robustness is shown, and the stated parameters were not the optimum.
pool.our_data_mapping: Compute a new feature for every existing signal row in all three sets. It is only a feature, so the cash minutes are valid even for the real (futures) set. Steps: load mins, daily, nifty, lot = H.minute_data() once. k = the signal minute's offset from 09:15. sigma_k = mean over the previous 14 sessions of |close at minute k / that day's 09:15 open - 1|. Ref = max(open_day, prev_close) for longs and min(...) for shorts; open_day/prev_close are in the real set, or take them from the minutes and daily data. noise_x = (price/Ref - 1)/sigma_k for longs and (1 - price/Ref)/sigma_k for shorts. Four settings to pick from on 12 May-31 Aug: (1) s_fable_op>=75 AND noise_x>=1.0, exit T3; (2) the same with noise_x>=1.5 (paper's VM 1.5); (3) s_opus_v3>=75 AND noise_x>=1.0, exit T1; (4) score = s_fable_op + 10*clip(noise_x-1,0,2), thr 75, T3. Minute data begin 15 Oct 2025, so the first 1-2 unseen sessions have only 12-13 lookback days; use what exists, and use 14 days, not 90.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial. Fable-OP's 'move today in daily ATRs' (30 pts) and Opus's 'move from the open' both measure the size of the move. Neither is normalised by time of day, and neither uses the max(open, prev close) gap reference. The per-month gates over 22 features did not include it.
pool.why_it_could_beat: A 0.6 % move at 09:25 and at 13:30 are very different events: the stock's average absolute move from the open grows through the day. Fable-OP gives points for 'early' signals, exactly where daily-ATR scaling is least informative. The band asks whether the move is abnormal for this stock at this minute, which is the paper's definition of a real imbalance. It should cut early-session fake breakouts and late-session drifts that are only noise.
pool.risks: Could be redundant with the existing ATR-move and from_open terms. The thresholds must be chosen on the design window only. Single-stock minute paths are noisier than SPY's, so sigma_k needs at least 14 days of clean minutes, and missing minutes need forward-fill.

pool.name: Nifty noise-area state as an intraday market filter (index-level intraday momentum: Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon; Gao, Han, Li & Zhou; Baltussen et al.)
pool.published_rules: Same noise bands as candidate 2, applied to the index (SPY): long when above UpperBound, short when below LowerBound, flat inside, decisions at HH:00/HH:30. FAQ Q21: making intraday shorts conditional on the index being below its 100/150/200-day SMA 'sacrifices a substantial portion of overall profitability', so the intraday state beats the daily-trend state. Gao et al. (JFE 2018): the first half-hour return (previous close to 10:00) predicts the last half-hour return.
pool.published_params: 14-day lookback, VM 1, 30-minute checks. Gao et al.: half-hour returns, with the first half-hour measured from the previous close.
pool.claimed_performance: SPY noise-area results as in candidate 2. Gao et al., SPY 1993-2013: slope 6.94 (x100), R2 1.6 %, out-of-sample R2 1.2 % (1.8 % with r12). Timing on the sign of r1 earns 6.67 %/yr, sd 6.19 %, Sharpe 1.08. The effect is stronger on high-volume, high-volatility, recession and macro-news days, and holds for 10 other ETFs. Baltussen et al. (JFE 2021): present in 60+ futures 1974-2020, stronger when dealer gamma is negative; their list has no Indian index. Limkriangkrai et al. (PBFJ 2023): strong in China and Japan, weak in Korea, absent in Hong Kong and Singapore; India was not tested.
pool.our_data_mapping: Use the Nifty index minutes from H.minute_data() and the previous close from H.regime()['prev']. At each signal minute, label Nifty UP (> UB), DOWN (< LB) or NOISE, with sigma from the previous 14 sessions of Nifty minutes. Four settings: (1) Fable-OP>=75, T3: longs only when Nifty is not DOWN; shorts only when Nifty is DOWN, which replaces setup B's fixed nifty_chg <= -0.25 % by applying the extra condition to B rows; (2) the same on Opus v3 with T1; (3) take the trade only when the Nifty state agrees with the side, else skip; (4) an ex-ante 'switch': Fable-OP T3 when the Nifty state agrees with the side, Opus v3 T1 when NOISE. Works on all three sets because it only filters existing rows.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial. A regime switch by the Nifty 20/50-day averages and by the 20-day change was tried (that is daily trend, not the intraday state). Setup B already requires Nifty down >= 0.25 %, and Fable-OP rewards 'stock moving without the index' (15 pts), which this filter partly contradicts. Switch-1 was chosen with hindsight; setting 4 is an ex-ante analogue.
pool.why_it_could_beat: B's fixed -0.25 % is time-blind: it is a big move at 09:20 and noise at 14:00. The band adapts to the time of day and to the gap. Breakout longs on days when the index is trending down beyond noise are the classic failure case, and the papers show the intraday index state carries information the daily trend does not.
pool.risks: No Indian test of index intraday momentum was found, and APAC evidence is mixed. It may cut trades sharply on trending days. Conflicts with Fable-OP's 'without the index' component. Index momentum is mainly a last-half-hour effect in Gao et al., so the transfer to stock breakouts at 09:17-14:15 is an extrapolation.

pool.name: 5-minute opening-range breakout on 'stocks in play' ranked by opening relative volume (Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz 2024)
pool.published_rules: Filters: open > $5, 14-day average volume >= 1M shares, 14-day ATR > $0.50. RelativeVolume_{t,j} = ORVolume_{t,j} / ((1/14) x sum over i=1..14 of ORVolume_{t-i,j}), where ORVolume is the volume of the first 5 minutes. Keep stocks with RelativeVolume >= 100 %, and trade the top 20 by RelativeVolume. Direction comes from the first 5-minute candle: if bullish, only a buy-stop at the 5-minute high; if bearish, only a sell-stop at the 5-minute low; a doji gets no order. Stop loss at 10 % of the 14-day ATR from the fill. No target: exit at the stop or the close (16:00). Size so that a stop-out loses 1 % of capital, with leverage capped at 4x.
pool.published_params: OR = 5 minutes (15/30/60 tested and worse), RVOL lookback 14 days, RVOL >= 1, top 20, stop 0.10 x ATR14, end-of-day exit, 1 % risk per trade.
pool.claimed_performance: US stocks 2016-2023, net of $0.0035/share commission only (no slippage modelled): the base ORB on all stocks made 29 % total, Sharpe 0.48, 41.4 % hit, MDD 13 %. ORB + RelVol top 20 made 1,637 %, IRR 41.6 %, Sharpe 2.81, MDD 12 %, worst day -1.61 %, alpha 35.8 %, beta 0. 15-min OR: Sharpe 1.43; 30-min: 0.21; 60-min: 0.40. Average R per trade is -0.02R for RVOL < 1, +0.08R for RVOL > 1 and +0.38R for RVOL > 30x. Per-stock win rates are about 17-24 %. There is no out-of-sample period. The QuantConnect rebuild covers only 2016 (Sharpe 2.40, 1,000-stock universe). Independent reviews found no post-2023 test. An arXiv study of ORB on Micro Nasdaq futures 2021-2025 found nothing significant out of sample. A search result describes a pre-registered practitioner rebuild reporting -0.0855R per trade over 2020-2026 after fill costs; it is on GitHub and was not opened, so it is unverified.
pool.our_data_mapping: A new generator on cash minutes from H.minute_data(). OR = the 09:15-09:19 IST candles. RVOL5 = the sum of volume 09:15-09:19 / the mean of the same over the previous 14 sessions. Direction = sign(close 09:19 - open 09:15). At 09:20, rank stocks with RVOL5 >= 1 and keep the top 6, the daily cap. Each gets a one-sided stop entry: the first minute whose high > OR high (low < OR low for shorts); fill at the next minute's open (scanner convention); orders not filled are cancelled at 14:15. ATR14 comes from daily candles up to the previous day only. Price with scanner.equity.fills.run_policies(close_at_eod=True), lots_for, costs.round_trip + costs.slippage(..., 0.02), EqConfig(), and Rs 15,000 risk. Four settings: (a) stop = OR opposite extreme clamped to [0.3, 0.9] ATR, exit CLOSE; (b) the same with exit CLOSE_TR; (c) 15-minute OR (the paper's runner-up), same stop, CLOSE; (d) stop 0.3 ATR, exit T3. Compare on unseen and known only (cash stand-in). Real 2nd-half futures cannot be generated, but cash candles for 1 Sep-11 Nov 2026 can be reported alongside.
pool.already_tried_overlap: The generator is new: the scanner's A/B need day-change thresholds, a previous-day high/low break, RSI bands and so on. The relative-volume idea overlaps the v3 rel_vol gate, but the scanner's rel_vol is cumulative volume against a 5-session profile, not the first-5-minute volume against 14 sessions.
pool.why_it_could_beat: It trades a different, earlier slice of the day: the opening drive in names with abnormal opening interest. The scanner often fires only after a 0.6-0.9 % day move is already in. Fable-OP's own components (early in the session, at the extreme, moving without the index) say early idiosyncratic moves pay. Opening RVOL was the single factor that turned a Sharpe 0.48 base strategy into 2.81.
pool.risks: (1) Costs: the paper's 0.1-ATR stop costs about 0.3R a trade on NSE futures (STT 0.05 % sell side plus 0.02 %/side slippage, about 0.096 % of notional), against a published edge of about 0.08R, so the stop must be widened, which changes the strategy. (2) Correlation: opening direction is market-wide, so all 6 can stop the same morning, about -90k plus costs, beyond the 1.25 x -41,636 = -52k limit; consider at most 3 per side, which is within the rules. (3) A 17-24 % win rate means long losing streaks. (4) The first NSE candle carries the 09:08 call-auction price. (5) Large notional per trade means heavy margin. (6) No out-of-sample evidence anywhere, and independent checks so far are negative.

pool.name: Opening relative-volume ('stocks in play') gate on BOTH sides of the existing signals (Zarattini-Barbon-Aziz RVOL buckets; Parthasarathy 2019 on India: high-volume moves continue, low-volume moves reverse)
pool.published_rules: Zarattini-Barbon-Aziz: RelativeVolume = first-5-minute volume / its 14-day average, a hard gate at >= 100 %, then rank by RelativeVolume. Parthasarathy (Review of Behavioral Finance 2019, Indian stocks, method of Pritamani & Singal 2001): large one-day price changes on low volume are followed by reversals (a contrarian strategy earns significant short-horizon profits), while large changes on high volume continue over the following 20 days. The abstract gives no thresholds, and the full text is paywalled.
pool.published_params: RVOL lookback 14 days, threshold 1.0 (with buckets up to 30x). The Indian study's volume thresholds are not disclosed in the abstract.
pool.claimed_performance: ORB average R by opening RVOL: -0.02R (< 1), +0.08R (> 1), +0.38R (> 30x), US 2016-2023 in sample. India (Parthasarathy): continuation after high-volume and reversal after low-volume large moves, daily horizon; no magnitudes in the abstract.
pool.our_data_mapping: Compute rvol5 for every signal row from minute data: the 09:15-09:19 volume / the mean over the previous 14 sessions. This is known from 09:20; for 09:17-09:19 signals use the scanner's rel_vol or skip them. Four settings: (1) s_fable_op>=75 AND rvol5>=1 on both sides, T3; (2) Opus v3 with the rel_vol>=1 gate extended to shorts (feature already in all sets), T1; (3) s_fable_op + 10 x [rvol5>=2], thr 75, T3; (4) (1) using the scanner's own rel_vol instead of rvol5.
pool.already_tried_overlap: HIGH. v3 is exactly a rel_vol<1 gate on longs, and per-month gates over 22 features likely included rel_vol. New elements: applying it to shorts, and the opening-only 14-session measure. Expect a small gain at best.
pool.why_it_could_beat: Shorts have no volume gate today. The Indian daily evidence and the US intraday evidence both say breaks on thin volume tend to revert. That fits Opus v3 losing on unseen, where its short book is unfiltered.
pool.risks: Largely redundant with v3, so gains may be noise. The Indian study is daily-horizon and its thresholds are unknown. A gate removes trades, so per-day caps fill with later, possibly worse signals.

pool.name: Volatility-state day filter (ORB / intraday-momentum payoffs rise with volatility: Lundström; Gao et al.; Limkriangkrai et al.; Concretum VIX buckets)
pool.published_rules: Gao et al.: sort days into terciles by first-half-hour realised volatility (from 1-minute returns inside the first 30 minutes). Predictability is minimal in the low tercile (R2 0.6 %, r1 insignificant), 1.0 % in the middle and 3.3 % in the high tercile. Lundström (Umeå WP 861, rev. 2017): average daily ORB returns by volatility state, with the highest-minus-lowest state about 150 bps/day for S&P 500 futures and about 200 bps/day for crude oil. Limkriangkrai et al.: volatility drives intraday momentum more than volume. Concretum Fig. 8: Sharpe rises with VIX at the open, from about 1.5 to about 3.5 at VIX > 40, then falls.
pool.published_params: Tercile split on first-30-minute realised volatility (Gao); volatility-state buckets (Lundström; the abstract does not give the construction).
pool.claimed_performance: Gao et al.: R2 0.6 % vs 3.3 % in the low vs high volatility tercile, SPY 1993-2013, with out-of-sample R2 positive overall. Lundström: about 150 bps/day spread on S&P futures (abstract only; the PDF host was unavailable). Concretum: Sharpe increasing in VIX (in sample).
pool.our_data_mapping: Build an ex-ante day state from Nifty minutes. RV30 = sqrt(sum of squared 1-minute log returns 09:15-09:44), compared with its median over the previous 20 sessions; this is known at 09:45, so apply it to signals at or after 09:45. For signals before 09:45 use the prior-day state: Nifty previous-day true range / Nifty ATR14 from daily data up to t-1. India VIX is NOT cached, so realised volatility only. Four settings: (1) skip all signals on low-volatility days (ratio < 0.8, or the bottom tercile of the design window); (2) on low-volatility days use Opus v3 T1, otherwise Fable-OP T3 (an ex-ante, volatility-based analogue of Switch-1); (3) the prior-day TR/ATR < 0.8 version for all signals; (4) skip only Fable-OP longs on low-volatility days. Filters existing rows, so it works on real, unseen and known.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Not tried. Regimes by Nifty 20/50-day averages and by 20-day change were trend measures, not volatility. Fable-OP's 'move in daily ATRs' is stock-level, not market-volatility state.
pool.why_it_could_beat: Fable-OP's T3 (2.6R) needs real trend days, and published evidence says breakouts and intraday momentum pay mostly in high-volatility sessions. On quiet days T1 or no trade should lose less, which targets the drawdown and worst-day bar.
pool.risks: Few days per tercile means a high overfitting risk; fix the cut on 12 May-31 Aug only. Index-level results may not carry over to single-stock breakouts. The Lundström magnitude is from the abstract only.

pool.name: Last-half-hour exit rule: cut shorts at 15:00 and hold longs only with market intraday momentum (Baltussen, Da & Soebhag end-of-day reversal; Gao et al. market intraday momentum)
pool.published_rules: End-of-day reversal (Baltussen, Da & Soebhag, working paper Sept 2026): ROD3 = the stock return from the previous close to 15:00 (overnight + first half-hour + middle of day, skipping 15:00-15:30). LH = the last half-hour (15:30-16:00). Sort stocks into quintiles or deciles on ROD3 and hold during LH: low-ROD3 (intraday losers) beat high-ROD3. The effect is 'entirely driven by the subsample with negative ROD3 returns' and holds in the largest and most liquid stocks. Gao et al.: the market's first half-hour return (from the previous close) and its 12th half-hour return predict the last half-hour with the same sign.
pool.published_params: Predictor window: previous close to 30 minutes before the close's preceding half-hour (ROD3); hold window: the last 30 minutes. Gao: r1 = previous close to 10:00, r12 = 15:00-15:30, r13 = 15:30-16:00.
pool.claimed_performance: EOD reversal, US 1993-2024: value-weighted low-minus-high quintile 3.55 bps/day (t = 11.05), 6-factor alpha 3.43 bps; equal-weighted 5.81 bps/day (t = 17.75). The bottom-decile losers gain 4.8 bps in LH, top-decile winners about 0. Present in almost every 5-year rolling window. Gao: timing on the sign of r1 gives Sharpe 1.08, out-of-sample R2 1.2 %. No Indian evidence for either.
pool.our_data_mapping: NSE closes at 15:30, so LH = the 15:00-15:29 candles. Re-simulate open positions with cash minutes from H.minute_data(), applied on top of the baseline/candidate exit (T3, CLOSE, CLOSE_TR). At 14:59 close, every SHORT still open exits; scanner shorts are intraday losers by construction (day_chg >= 0.9 % down). A LONG still open holds to 15:29 only if Nifty's return from the previous close to 14:59 is positive (market intraday momentum), otherwise it exits at 14:59. Settings: (1) shorts-only cut; (2) shorts cut plus the long momentum condition; (3) cut everything at 14:59; (4) (2) applied to Fable-OP CLOSE_TR. Clean on unseen and known (cash); on real it can only be approximated, because the real set is futures.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None tried. Interacts with candidate 1: it matters only for exits that can still be open at 15:00 (T3, CLOSE, *_TR).
pool.why_it_could_beat: The scanner's short book is exactly the 'intraday loser' group where the papers find the late rebound (retail buy-the-dip and short covering into the close). Exiting before it removes a systematic adverse drift at no extra cost, since the exit happens anyway.
pool.risks: The effect is tiny: about 5 bps against a trade risk of roughly 50-100 bps, so at most about 0.05-0.1R on trades still open at 15:00, which may be lost in noise. NSE's official close is the VWAP of 15:00-15:30, and the expiry-day settlement window may change last-half-hour behaviour. Market intraday momentum is absent in some Asian markets (HK, Singapore) and weak in Sweden, and was never tested on Nifty in anything I could open.

pool.name: CPR width and two-day pivot relationship as a per-stock trend-day filter (Pivot Boss method, widely used by Indian intraday traders)
pool.published_rules: CPR is computed from the prior day's H, L, C: Pivot = (H+L+C)/3, BC = (H+L)/2, TC = (Pivot - BC) + Pivot. Whichever is higher is labelled TC. Width = TC - BC. Ochoa (Secrets of a Pivot Boss, ch. 6, read through a blog transcript): an extremely tight CPR means the prior period was sideways, which 'usually leads to breakout or trending behaviour' next session. 'Most trending days occur when the central pivot range is considerably tighter than the prior day's range', especially after an unusually wide prior range. Expected day types are Trend, Double-Distribution Trend or Extended Typical. A wide CPR means Typical, Trading-Range or Sideways. Pivot Range Histogram: a reading below 0.5 means trending, below 0.25 strongly trending, above 0.75 sideways. Two-day relationships: Higher Value (today's BC above yesterday's TC) is the most bullish, so buy pullbacks if the open confirms. Overlapping Higher is moderately bullish. Lower Value is the most bearish, so sell rallies. Overlapping Lower is moderately bearish. Outside Value (today's CPR engulfs yesterday's) means sideways. Inside Value, especially when much narrower than yesterday's, means a breakout or trend day. Unchanged depends on where the day opens. Indian practitioner pages repeat 'narrow CPR = trending day, wide = sideways' without numeric thresholds.
pool.published_params: Histogram cut-offs 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75. The histogram's normalisation code (book appendix) was not in the transcript. Indian pages use inconsistent TC/BC formulas, so pin one definition before testing.
pool.claimed_performance: No backtest of CPR width or two-day relationships was found anywhere. The book's only statistics are from YM (Dow mini) futures, Nov 2008-Jun 2009, 165 days, in-sample: the central pivot was touched on 63% of days and S1/R1 on 73.3%. The ~37% of days that never touched the pivot were 'usually trending days'. A TradingView dashboard says it forward-tests the narrow-CPR trend-day hit rate but publishes no numbers.
pool.our_data_mapping: Use daily candles from H.minute_data(), using only rows before the signal day. For day d, take day d-1's H/L/C for today's CPR and day d-2's for yesterday's CPR. Let top = max(TC, BC) and bot = min(TC, BC). width_pct = (top - bot) / P * 100. w_rank = percentile rank of width_pct among the stock's previous 20 sessions, standing in for the Pivot Range Histogram. w_vs_rng = (top - bot) / (H[d-1] - L[d-1]). relation is one of HV, OHV, LV, OLV, IV, OV or UV. Four settings to declare in advance: S1 drops signals with w_rank > 0.75. S2 keeps longs only on HV/OHV/IV and shorts only on LV/OLV/IV. S3 = S1 + S2. S4 drops signals with w_rank > 0.5. Apply each on top of (s_fable_op, 75, T3, 6) and (s_opus_v3, 75, T1, 6) as a function spec, picking on real 12 May-31 Aug. Daily data starts Jan 2024, so all three sets (real, unseen, known) can be tested.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None directly. The regime switch tried used Nifty 20/50-day averages for the whole market; this filter is per stock and uses pivot geometry. The previous-day-high/low break is already part of setups A and B, so a price-above-TC location rule would be redundant and is left out.
pool.why_it_could_beat: The system earns on stock-level trend days, and both baselines lose mainly on choppy days that hit the stop. CPR width and pivot migration estimate each stock's trend-day odds before the open from information that is absent from the 21 harness features (no prior-day range or pivot feature exists). Dropping wide-CPR days could cut stops without touching the strongest days.
pool.risks: No published statistics; this is folklore-grade evidence. Likely correlated with atr_pct, ret5 and vs20. Filters can leave fewer than 6 trades on good days and lower the total even when per-trade P&L improves. A narrow CPR can also simply mean continued low volatility (volatility clustering).

pool.name: Prior-day compression: NR7 / NR4 / inside day before a previous-day-high or low break (Crabel; Unofficed F&O backtest)
pool.published_rules: Unofficed (Indian F&O watchlist): NR7 means the day had the narrowest range of the last 7 days. The refinement is an NR7 that is also an inside bar. 'Long if the previous day's high is broken with stop loss at the previous day's low. Short if the previous day's low is broken with stop loss at the previous day's high.' No target is given; examples enter at the start of the day. ID/NR4 (Crabel): an inside day that is also the narrowest of the last 4 bars. Place a buy stop above its high and a sell stop below its low, with the stop loss at the opposite end. Cancel if the next bar does not trigger.
pool.published_params: Lookbacks 7 (NR7) and 4 (NR4). Inside bar = lower high and higher low than the prior bar. Universe: NSE F&O stocks. Exits tested by Unofficed: same-day, next day, and 5 days.
pool.claimed_performance: Unofficed Python backtest, F&O stocks showing NR7+IB from 2015 to the writing date, 2,238 setups. Results are summed 'pl_points' (not normalised; costs not stated; in-sample; no OOS). Intraday: buys net +278,052 (546 up / 611 down); sells net +1,057,878 (642 up / 484 down, average win 4,583 vs average loss -3,893). Next day: buys +626,661, sells +226,257. 5-day: buys +1,087,522, sells +412,299. Author's conclusion: shorts work best intraday, longs work best next-day or positional. No statistics from Crabel's book were found online.
pool.our_data_mapping: From daily candles before day d: rng = H - L. NR7 flag if rng[d-1] == min(rng[d-7..d-1]); NR4 likewise over 4 days. ID flag if H[d-1] < H[d-2] and L[d-1] > L[d-2]. cr = rng[d-1] / ATR14[d-1]. Setups A and B already require breaking the previous day's high (A) or low (B), which is exactly the Unofficed trigger. Keep our structural stop, not the much wider opposite-end stop. Four settings: S1 adds 10 to the score (s_fable_op or s_opus_v3) when the prior day is NR7 or ID/NR4, so 65-74 signals enter on compressed days. S2 drops signals when cr > 1.5 (the prior day was wide-range, which Ochoa expects to be followed by a sideways day). S3 keeps shorts (B) only after NR7 or ID; longs unchanged. S4 = S1 + S2. All three sets are covered.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None. Harness features describe only today's range (pos, range_atr) and 5/20-day returns. Prior-day range compression was never used.
pool.why_it_could_beat: The setups trade the break of the prior day's range, and when that range is compressed the break is a volatility-expansion event rather than noise inside a wide range. The Unofficed asymmetry (shorts strongest intraday) matches setup B, the side where Opus v3 does worst on unseen. Day-level gating could also lower the worst day.
pool.risks: NR7 or ID days are rare (about one day in 7 per stock, fewer with the inside-bar condition), so a 126-session set yields small samples, and the bonus form (S1) is safer than a hard filter. The evidence is unnormalised points, in-sample, with costs unstated. Volatility clustering argues the other way.

pool.name: Open = Low / Open = High (OHL) confirmation of breakout signals
pool.published_rules: TradingQnA (quoting a popular Indian article): 'Find the scrips with open = low and they are your BUY scrips; open = high are your SHORT SELL scrips. Enter the trade after 15-30 minutes of trade if the opening low is not breached.' Kotak Neo: stop just below the day's low, high-volume stocks only, minimum RR 1:2, confirm with above-average volume. BTST variant: after 15:25 buy open=low F&O stocks and exit at the next day's close.
pool.published_params: Tolerance for open == low is not defined (exact match implied). Check time is 15-30 minutes after the open. Universe: F&O stocks.
pool.claimed_performance: TradingQnA, F&O stocks, 2007-2018, no costs, in-sample: the intraday version had 'just 50% accuracy with a risk reward ratio of 1.3', about breakeven after costs. The BTST version was 'much better' (summed returns 22,350%, about 28 trades a day). That version holds overnight, so it does not fit this intraday system. A forum reply says traders often abandon OHL for its high failure rate. A vendor page claimed 55-58% win rate and PF 1.35 for open=low longs on Nifty 50 F&O stocks, 2018-24, but this was seen only in a search snippet. The page could not be read, so the claim is not counted.
pool.our_data_mapping: Per signal, compute the day's low L_t and high H_t from 09:15 to the signal minute. Unseen/known: from H.minute_data() cash candles. Real: derivable without minute data, since range = range_atr * atr_pct / 100 * price, low = price - pos * range for longs (high = price + pos * range for shorts), and open = price / (1 + from_open/100) for longs (sign flipped for shorts). OL flag (long): L_t >= open * (1 - tol). OH flag (short): H_t <= open * (1 + tol). Four settings: S1 filters longs to OL and shorts to OH with tol = 0.05%. S2 is S1 with tol = 0.15%. S3 adds 10 to the score instead of filtering. S4 applies S1 only to signals with minutes_since_open >= 15. Apply to the Fable-OP/T3 and Opus v3/T1 specs.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial. Opus scores the move from the open and a small gap, and pos measures place in today's range. 'Never traded beyond the open against the trade' is a path condition that no feature captures.
pool.why_it_could_beat: A stock that never traded below its open shows one-sided demand from the first print. Breakouts on such days should follow through better than breakouts on days that first flushed through the open, which are two-sided and choppier, and choppy days produce most of the stop-outs. The rule is cheap and has a single parameter.
pool.risks: The only Indian number (50% at 1.3 RR) is near breakeven. For signals in the first minutes the condition is nearly automatic. Results are sensitive to the tolerance. The cash open differs from the futures open, which carries a premium, so compute on the traded instrument where possible.

pool.name: Sector relative-strength confirmation (trade the strong stock in the strong sector, short the weak stock in the weak sector)
pool.published_rules: Chartink (Indian practitioner): RS = stock RSI - index RSI, or ranking by 5-day outperformance versus NIFTY. Stock and index must use the same indicator and timeframe (for example 15-minute vs 15-minute). Positive means stronger than the index. The common Indian intraday practice of trading the strong stock in the strong sector has no published intraday rules or statistics. md0n repo: sector/size rotation (top 2 of 13 indices, monthly).
pool.published_params: No intraday parameters published. Chartink example: TCS RSI 55.30 vs NIFTY 48.93 gives RS +6.37.
pool.claimed_performance: No intraday sector-RS backtest was found. md0n (monthly sector rotation, 2007-2026): CAGR 12.1% vs 9.5%, max drawdown -48.3%, verdict 'Fail, lost in-sample'. Peer-reviewed industry-momentum and lead-lag studies (Moskowitz-Grinblatt; Hou) appeared in search results but could not be opened, and they work at monthly or daily horizons, not intraday.
pool.our_data_mapping: A sector map already exists in the repo: /home/user/indian_breakout_scanner/config/nifty_largemidcap250_fallback.csv, 'Industry' column. It covers 190 of the 218 minute-data symbols. 28 need manual tags: AMBER, ANANDRATHI, ANGELONE, ATHERENERG, BANDHANBNK, CAMS, CDSL, CROMPTON, CUB, DATAPATTNS, DELHIVERY, FORCEMOT, ICICILIFE, IEX, INOXWIND, KARURVYSYA, KAYNES, KFINTECH, MANAPPURAM, NAVINFLUOR, NBCC, PGEL, PNBHOUSING, RBLBANK, SAGILITY, SONACOMS, SYRMA, UJJIVANSFB. Consider splitting 'Financial Services' (44 names) into banks, NBFC, capital markets and insurance. At the signal minute t, compute each sector's median % change versus the previous close from minute closes up to t (no look-ahead). sector_rs = sector_median - nifty_chg. Four settings: S1 keeps longs only if sector_rs > 0 and shorts only if sector_rs < 0. S2 keeps longs only if the sector is top-3 by median change and shorts only if bottom-3. S3 adds 10 to the score when aligned and subtracts 10 when opposed. S4 = S1 plus the stock leading its sector (direction-adjusted day_chg - sector_median > 0). This needs one pass over the minute data for all three sets.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial. Fable-OP's 'stock moving without the index' (15 points) compares the stock with Nifty, not with its sector. crowd_same and breadth_dir (real set only) measure market breadth, not sector. No sector feature was ever used.
pool.why_it_could_beat: Sector-wide flows (institutional sector bets, peer news, commodity moves for metals and oil) persist within the day. A breakout with a sector tailwind should reach T1 to T3 more often than one fighting its sector. It also spreads the 6 daily slots across sectors, which can lower the worst day.
pool.risks: No intraday evidence; the only costed Indian test (monthly rotation) failed. It can conflict with Fable-OP's idiosyncratic-move component, which may be the real edge. Sectors with 1 to 4 members are noisy. Extra engineering is needed to join the minute data.

pool.name: Stocks-in-Play relative volume: extend the rel_vol gate to shorts and weight the score by rel_vol
pool.published_rules: Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz (2024, SSRN 4729284): price > $5, 14-day average volume >= 1M shares, ATR14 > $0.50. Relative Volume of the opening 5 minutes versus the 14-day average must be at least 100%, and only the top 20 by RV are traded. Direction follows the first 5-minute candle, with a stop order at the opening-range high or low. Stop loss is 10% of ATR14; no target; exit at the close. Risk 1% per trade, 4x leverage cap, $0.0035 per share commission. School Run test (Nifty 100, since 2015): stop-and-reverse on the 09:30-09:45 candle, up to 4 re-entries, square-off at the close, 0.05% round-trip cost.
pool.published_params: RV >= 1.0; top 20 by RV; stop = 0.10 x ATR14; exit at the close; opening range of 5, 15, 30 or 60 minutes.
pool.claimed_performance: US, 2016-2023, more than 7,000 stocks, in-sample: average P&L -0.02R per trade at RV < 100%, +0.08R at RV > 100%, +0.38R at RV > 30x. The top-20 Stocks-in-Play 5-minute ORB returned over 1,600% net with Sharpe 2.81 and 36% annual alpha (S&P 198%). The base 5-minute ORB without the RV filter had Sharpe 0.48. Indian out-of-sample replication (md0n; Nifty 100; 15-minute ORB plus RV filter; Indian charges plus 0.05% slippage per side): +10.4% in one tuned year, then lost money in every out-of-sample year, -21.8% over 4 years. Gross profit was Rs 173 on 759 trades against Rs 2,357 of costs. School Run on Nifty 100 had a 28-38% win rate and 69-71 of 100 stocks net positive, mostly gross, with no aggregate numbers published.
pool.our_data_mapping: The harness already has rel_vol (volume so far / normal volume by time of day). Four settings: S1 is Opus v3 plus rel_vol < 1 scoring 0 for shorts too (T1). S2 is Fable-OP with rel_vol >= 1 on both sides (T3). S3 uses score' = s_fable_op + 10 * clip(log2(rel_vol), -1.5, 1.5) with threshold 75 and exit T3. S4 is S3 but with exit CLOSE_TR when rel_vol >= 2 (the Zarattini idea of holding a stock in play to the close with a stop), else T3, written as a function spec with a per-row pol.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Strong partial overlap: Opus v3 is exactly the rel_vol < 1 gate on longs. New here: gating shorts, continuous RV weighting, and a close-hold exit for very high RV.
pool.why_it_could_beat: The paper shows P&L rising steadily with RV. The short side (scored by Opus) is where Opus v3 lost on unseen, and volume-backed breakdowns are more likely news-driven and persistent. S4 lets the rare very-high-volume trend days run past T3.
pool.risks: The one costed Indian out-of-sample replication of RV-filtered ORB failed after costs. Zarattini measured opening 5-minute RV, not mid-session RV. Gains may already be priced into v3. It is easy to overfit the RV weighting.

pool.name: Scale-out exit: half the lots at T1, half trailed (T3_TR or CLOSE_TR)
pool.published_rules: Zarattini et al.: no profit target, a tight stop (10% ATR), exit at the close: 'let profits run as long as the trend persists'. Indian retail algo platforms (for example Stratzy on Dhan) sell variants with a fixed RR (1:2, 1:3) or a trailing stop loss (TSL). Kotak Neo advises booking quick profits at RR of at least 1:2. No published source compares partial booking plus a trail against a fixed target on Indian stocks.
pool.published_params: Split 50/50. Runner trails per the scanner's existing logic (stop to entry after T1, to T1 after T2, to T2 after T3, target T3 for T3_TR, close for CLOSE_TR).
pool.claimed_performance: No published head-to-head comparison found; the Dhan vendor pages show strategy names only, with no readable statistics. In the internal baselines, Opus v3/T1 and Fable-OP/T3 win in different regimes (unseen: Fable +78,849 vs Opus v3 -1,28,597; real 2nd half: Opus v3 +2,80,042 vs Fable +2,68,584). Switch-1 picks between them by regime with hindsight.
pool.our_data_mapping: No new simulation is needed. Add synthetic columns per set: net_SPLIT = 0.5*net_T1 + 0.5*net_T3_TR - ~24 (one extra exit order: Rs 20 brokerage plus GST). r_SPLIT is built the same way and status_T1 is unchanged. Alternatives: SPLIT_C = T1 with CLOSE_TR, SPLIT_2 = T1 with T2_TR. Then run H.compare with ('s_fable_op', 75, 'SPLIT', 6) and ('s_opus_v3', 75, 'SPLIT', 6). Lot granularity: unseen and known have a 'lots' column. Put floor(lots/2) at T1 and the rest on the runner. When lots == 1 use a declared single policy (T3_TR). Real has no lots column, so use the 50/50 approximation there and say so. Declare at most 4 combos (2 score models x 2 runner policies) and pick on real 12 May-31 Aug.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial. 'Stop to breakeven after 0.4-0.8R' was tried on the whole position, and the T2_TR/T3_TR/CLOSE_TR columns exist but were never compared systematically. A split position was never tried.
pool.why_it_could_beat: The two baselines are the same signals with different payoff shapes: T1 banks the frequent small win and T3 catches trend days. A split earns part of both on every trade without a hindsight-chosen regime switch. It should cut daily variance, which matters for the bar of worst day and drawdown within 1.25x of the better baseline.
pool.risks: An average of two policies usually lands between them, so it beats both only if the trailing runner adds value beyond plain T3. Lot rounding and the extra order cost are an issue for single-lot stocks, and the real set has no lot column.

pool.name: Stock F&O expiry-calendar filter (avoid longs on expiry and the day before, favour longs the day after)
pool.published_rules: Vipul (2005, Journal of Futures Markets 25(11), 1045-1065): compares price, volatility and volume of the underlying shares on the day before expiry (E-1), expiry (E) and the day after (E+1) against the same weekdays 1-2 weeks away (Wilcoxon test). Gupta, Metia & Trivedi (2003; 5 NSE stocks, 2001-03): tested abnormal volume, returns, reversal and pinning around option expiry.
pool.published_params: Event days E-1, E, E+1. Since 1 Sep 2025, NSE stock F&O monthly contracts expire on the last Tuesday of the month (previous trading day if it is a holiday). All three of our sets fall after that change.
pool.claimed_performance: Vipul: share prices 'dip slightly' on E-1 and rise significantly ('abnormally high') on E+1. Volume is abnormally high on E, building from E-1 to E+1 in shares with high derivative volume. He attributes this to arbitrage and short-sale limits in the Indian cash market. Gupta et al.: no statistically significant abnormal volume or returns and no pinning, except Satyam volume in 2002-03. arXiv 2507.04859 measures no day-before/day-after effect and only cites Vipul. All early-2000s, cash-settled era, in-sample.
pool.our_data_mapping: Build the expiry calendar from the trading days in the minute data: the last Tuesday of each month, rolled back across holidays. Flag E-1, E and E+1 per signal day. Four settings: S1 skips longs on E-1 and E. S2 skips all signals on E (roll and pinning noise; near-month liquidity moving to next month). S3 lowers the long threshold to 65 on E+1. S4 = S1 + S3. Overlay on both baselines.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None.
pool.why_it_could_beat: If arbitrage unwinds and roll flows still push prices down into expiry and up after it, a handful of calendar days can be avoided or favoured cheaply. Skipping chaotic expiry sessions may lower the worst day.
pool.risks: Very low statistical power: about 6 expiries per set, so 6-18 flagged days. The evidence is 20 years old, from before 2018-19 when stock derivatives moved to physical settlement, so the mechanism has changed, and a second study found no effect. High overfitting risk; treat as a tie-breaker only.

pool.name: Futures open-interest build-up confirmation (long build-up for longs, short build-up for shorts; skip short-covering rallies)
pool.published_rules: Zerodha Varsity table: price up with OI up = 'more trades on the long side (long build-up)'. Price down with OI down = long unwinding. Price down with OI up = short build-up. Price up with OI down = short covering. 'Abnormally high OI indicates high leverage. Beware.' The chapter gives no thresholds, entries or exits. In comments the author prefers end-of-day OI for strategies and flags doubts about the accuracy of intraday OI.
pool.published_params: None published.
pool.claimed_performance: None. No Indian backtest of the four-quadrant OI rules was found. Indian academic work on OI predictability (index futures, stock options) is mixed.
pool.our_data_mapping: Not possible with cached data. The cached minute candles are cash (oi = 0). The only NSE_FO key in replay_sep/minutes.pkl (NSE_FO|61471, from 26 Aug 2026, oi > 0) appears to be an index future (prices about 24,700, so probably Nifty), not a stock future. It would need either (a) a pre-open version: the previous day's stock-futures OI change from NSE F&O bhavcopy archives, giving a long/short build-up flag known before the open, or (b) futures minute candles with OI, keeping longs only if OI rose since the open and price is up, and shorts only if OI rose and price is down.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None.
pool.why_it_could_beat: It tells new positioning apart from short covering, which Indian traders believe fades quickly. Short-covering spikes are a plausible source of false long breakouts in setup A.
pool.risks: No published evidence of edge. Expiry-week rollover makes OI fall mechanically and look like unwinding. Intraday OI is a snapshot series that updates in bursts. Needs new data.

pool.name: Meta-labeling filter: regularized gradient-boosted trees stacked on both existing scores, label matched to the exit, Platt-calibrated, top-quantile gate
pool.published_rules: Lopez de Prado meta-labeling, as quoted in the Singh & Joubert appendix: a primary model with high recall fixes the side. Its features are concatenated with its prediction to form the secondary model's inputs. The meta-label is 1 when the primary trade's triple-barrier outcome is profitable, else 0. Trade only when the secondary model says 1 (p>0.5 in Hudson & Thames), and use the probability for size. AFML also says separate long-only and short-only meta-models are legitimate. Hudson & Thames: a random-forest meta-model on SMA 20/50 and Bollinger 1.5-sigma primaries for E-mini, with the minority class up-sampled. Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk (2024): label = signal reaches a +4% take-profit. They fit 5 classifiers (MLP, AdaBoost, HistGradientBoosting, SGD, logistic) and combine them by soft vote, with HistGB at double weight. Trade only if p >= P2, where P2 = the 90th percentile of validation-set probabilities, so about 10% of signals are taken.
pool.published_params: Hudson & Thames: random forest, max_depth and n_estimators grid-searched (final values not reported). Features: 15/31/50-bar volatility, autocorrelation lags 1-5, momentum 1-5. Out-of-sample 2018-01 to 2019-01. Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk: train on the first 1,500 days from 2000, test 2006-2022, 0.05% cost per side. P2 = 0.60 for the ensemble and 0.68 for HistGB alone. sklearn: isotonic calibration is not recommended with far fewer than 1,000 calibration samples, so use sigmoid (Platt).
pool.claimed_performance: Positive. Hudson & Thames, E-mini, out-of-sample: precision 0.48 to 0.54 for trend-following and 0.17 to 0.20 for mean reversion; accuracy 48% to 55% and 17% to 63%. The Sharpe tables are images that could not be read; the text says trend-following won only on a risk-adjusted basis. Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk (arXiv working paper, US equities, out-of-sample 2006-2022): validation precision 0.653 for HistGB against a 0.541 base rate (logistic 0.580). The full strategy's IR* was 1.30 against 0.14 for the benchmark, but the authors changed other things at the same time, and excluding two stocks cut the annual return from 49% to 11%. Negative. QuantConnect forum (Baldisserri): meta-model added no return over a single end-to-end model and gave a lower average Sharpe. MQL5 RSI on EURUSD, trained on 790 signals, tested 2022-2024: profit factor 0.93 to 0.72 (the filtered strategy was worse). Lund thesis: the non-meta model had the better Sharpe. Interactive ML toy: a meta-model that sees only the primary's score is the same as raising the threshold (AP 0.809 vs 0.809); gains come only from information the primary lacks. Overall, the published lift is +3 to +6 precision points at best and often zero or negative with fewer than about 1,000 training signals.
pool.our_data_mapping: Universe: all A/B rows (about 35 a day, the high-recall primary AFML prescribes), not just rows scoring 75 or more; that subset is only about 165 design rows. Features: the 21 COMMON columns, side (0/1), s_opus, s_fable_op, a one-hot of the pre-open regime label, and r20 from H.regime(). Add crowd counts computed from the signal set itself up to the signal minute (same-side signals so far today, opposite-side so far, same-minute count). These work in unseen too, unlike REAL_ONLY crowd_same. Labels: y=1[r_T3>0] for a T3 exit (41% positive on 12 May-31 Aug). Do not use T3-hit, which is only 3.5% positive. For a T1 exit, y=1[r_T1>0] (46%). Model: lightgbm LGBMClassifier with num_leaves=7, max_depth=3, min_child_samples=80, learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=300, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.7, reg_lambda=10, path_smooth=20, and monotone_constraints +1 on s_opus and s_fable_op only. Calibrate with CalibratedClassifierCV(method='sigmoid', cv=GroupKFold(5) splits by day), on the design window only. Gate: p >= the quantile of out-of-fold design p that matches the baseline's selection rate (top 6% for T3, the s_fable_op>=75 rate; top 8% for T1, the s_opus_v3>=75 rate). Then H.pick(n=6) in time order, spec ('p_meta', thr, 'T3', 6). Four settings declared in advance: (a) y=r_T3>0, exit T3, top 6%; (b) y=r_T1>0, exit T1, top 8%; (c) as (a) but LGBMRegressor with Huber loss on clip(r_T3,-1.2,2.6); (d) as (a) with sample_weight=|r_T3| (AFML return attribution).
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial: 'L2 logistic fits on ~20 snapshot features to predict reaching T1'. Differences: non-linear shallow trees, both baseline scores as inputs (stacking), crowd features from the signal list, label matched to the T3 exit, and a quantile gate. Setting (b) is the closest to what was tried; expect it to fail the same way if trees add nothing.
pool.why_it_could_beat: s_opus and s_fable_op are almost uncorrelated on the design window (rho = 0.04), so each holds information the other lacks, which is the condition under which meta-labeling helps. At the published best case, the T1 exit (about +/-1R) gains roughly 5 points of win rate, or about +0.1R a trade. That is about +Rs 1,200-1,500 a trade on roughly 300 trades, around Rs 4 lakh, the size of the gap between the baselines.
pool.risks: Trains on 2,746 rows from 78 days; the out-of-sample AUC will be noisy, and same-day signals are correlated. The closest negative case trained on a similar number of signals (790). The move from real futures to the cash stand-in shifts calibration; the quantile gate partly mitigates this. The total-net SE is about Rs 2.3 lakh for Fable-OP T3 and Rs 1.6 lakh for Opus v3 T1, so modest gains will not be statistically distinguishable.

pool.name: Two-score stacker (ensemble meta-labeling with at most 4 parameters per side)
pool.published_rules: Stack the primary predictions with a simple secondary model. AFML (via the Singh & Joubert appendix): 'develop an ML strategy exclusively for long positions ... and ... exclusively for short positions', meaning separate meta-models per side. Interactive ML: the meta-model adds value only in proportion to information the primary lacks. A meta-model on the primary's own score only is a monotone transform, the same as moving the threshold. Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk: soft-voting ensembles with the best model weighted higher beat both equal weights and the single best model (their RQ4).
pool.published_params: Interactive ML toy: a logistic meta-model with weights [1.58, 1.71] on [signal, regime]. Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk: HistGB double weight in a soft vote; gate at the 90th percentile of validation probabilities.
pool.claimed_performance: Interactive ML toy, synthetic: adding one feature the primary never used lifted precision at 0.6 recall from 0.780 to 0.926. The signal-only meta-model stayed at 0.780 (AP 0.809, the same as raising the threshold). Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk: the weighted ensemble beat the equal-weight and best-single variants on IR*/Sortino in the sensitivity analysis (Table 11, out-of-sample 2006-2022, US equities). There is no published intraday evidence.
pool.our_data_mapping: Per side, LogisticRegression(C=1.0) on standardized [s_opus, s_fable_op, s_opus*s_fable_op]; label 1[r_T3>0] for T3 or 1[r_T1>0] for T1; fit on 12 May-31 Aug real only (1,715 longs, 1,031 shorts). Gate at the top 6% (T3) or top 8% (T1) of design out-of-fold probabilities, then H.pick n=6. Settings: (a) per-side logit, T3, top 6%; (b) per-side logit, T1, top 8%; (c) zero-parameter rank average: p = mean of the design-window ECDF percentiles of s_opus and s_fable_op within side, T3; (d) (a) plus a pre-open regime one-hot. Uses only columns present in all three sets.

pool.name: Selection with Guaranteed Risk (SGR): pick the score threshold by a binomial risk bound instead of a round 75
pool.published_rules: Geifman & El-Yaniv (2017), Algorithm 1: sort the labelled sample S_m by confidence kappa. Binary-search k = ceil(log2 m) times over thresholds theta = kappa(x_z), with z starting at ceil((z_min + z_max)/2), z_min = 1, z_max = m. At each step compute the empirical selective risk r_hat on the accepted points (kappa >= theta) and the bound b* = B*(r_hat, delta/k, n_accepted), the binomial-tail (Clopper-Pearson type) upper bound. If b* < r*, set z_max = z (accept more); else z_min = z. Output theta with the guarantee P(true selective risk > b*) < delta. Chalkidis & Savani apply SGR to trading classifiers, using the max class probability as kappa and making no trade when the classifier abstains.
pool.published_params: delta = 0.001 in both papers. Coverage comes out of the bound: 37-63% for binary trading classifiers.
pool.claimed_performance: Chalkidis & Savani, metals futures, 30-minute bars, anchored walk-forward, slippage 0.3 ticks: selective beat non-selective in most cases. Sharpe 0.21 vs 0.02 (LR FS2), 0.28 vs -0.03 (LR FS4), 0.33 vs -0.35 (NN FS1), 0.57 vs -1.03 (ternary RF FS3). Exceptions: LSTM FS2 -0.81 vs -0.67, RF FS1 -1.61 vs -1.60. Accuracy rose in every case. Their results 'did not demonstrate any advantage of the richer feature sets'.
pool.our_data_mapping: Use kappa = s_fable_op for the T3 exit (or s_opus for T1, or the C2 probability). Risk = 1[net_P < 0] on design-window rows (12 May-31 Aug) above a minimal score. Set r* = the breakeven loss rate W/(W+L), where W and L are the mean win and mean loss in R under policy P on the design window, minus a 0.03 margin; use delta = 0.05. To respect within-day correlation, use the number of distinct days that have at least one accepted signal as the bound's sample size, or a day-block bootstrap of B*. The threshold found replaces 75 in ('s_fable_op', theta, 'T3', 6). Settings: (a) s_fable_op with T3; (b) s_opus_v3 with T1; (c) C2 probability with T3; (d) (a) with risk = 1[r_T3 <= -0.97] (stopped).
pool.already_tried_overlap: It is a threshold-choice method; tuning the threshold on the existing scores may have been tried informally. It is not on the brief's tried list. It needs no model fit when applied to existing scores.
pool.why_it_could_beat: It replaces an arbitrary 75 with a threshold that carries an explicit statistical margin against selecting losers, which usually means fewer and better trades. Among 'bet only when confident' methods, it has the most concrete published trading evidence (positive Sharpe flips in most walk-forward cases).
pool.risks: The bound assumes i.i.d. rows, which same-day clustering violates; the day-count correction makes it loose. With about 150-250 accepted design rows the bound may accept very few signals. The gain, if any, comes only from a better threshold, not new information.

pool.name: Calibrated-probability bet sizing (AFML 2*Phi(z)-1 or ECDF tiers), sizing down only
pool.published_rules: AFML chapter 10 (mlfinlab-port code): clip p to [1e-6, 1 - 1e-6]; z = (p - 1/K)/sqrt(p(1-p)); m = 2*Phi(z) - 1 (times the side); discretize m = round(m/step)*step, clipped to [-1, 1]; optionally average m over concurrently active bets. Meyer, Barziy & Joubert (JFDS 2023, abstract only): six sizing algorithms; calibration significantly improves fixed-function sizing, while data-fitted methods (ECDF percentile sizing, sigmoid optimal position sizing) gain nothing from it. MQL5 RSI: bet = clip((p - 0.5)/0.5, 0, 1). Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk: Kelly fraction f = 2P - 1.
pool.published_params: K = 2 classes; step size is a user choice (0 = continuous); Platt calibration with small samples.
pool.claimed_performance: MQL5 RSI, EURUSD, out-of-sample 2022-2024: bet sizing on the meta-filtered trades cut the max drawdown from -593 to -96 pips (P&L -577 to -86) but left profit factor at 0.72, so sizing shrinks losses without creating an edge. Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk: Kelly 2P-1 raised returns and volatility but did not raise IR* ('very limited impact'). Meyer et al.: 'significantly improved' for fixed methods; numbers not accessible (full text paywalled).
pool.our_data_mapping: Take calibrated p from C1 or C2. Two-tier ECDF sizing: full size if p >= q90 of design out-of-fold p; half size if q75 <= p < q90; skip below q75. Alternatively, size = min(1, m(p)/m(q90)) with step 0.5. New lots = max(1, floor(size*lots)), so risk never exceeds Rs 15,000, and keep max 6 trades a day. In the harness, a callable returns trades whose pnl = net_P * new_lots/lots. The unseen/known sets have a 'lots' column. The real set does not, so use net_P * size there (approximate), or re-cost exactly with scanner.equity.costs.round_trip.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None; position size has always been the full Rs 15,000 risk.
pool.why_it_could_beat: It lowers the threshold (more trades) while halving exposure on the marginal ones. That can keep the worst day and max drawdown within the 1.25x bar while adding some net profit if the marginal tier has small positive expectancy. It is a complement to C1/C2, not a standalone edge.

pool.name: VWAP trailing stop, no fixed target, square off at the close
pool.published_rules: Source: Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon, 'Beat the Market' (SFI WP 24-97, 2024/25), SPY on 1-minute bars. Entry: price leaves the 'Noise Area'. Entries are checked at HH:00 and HH:30 from 10:00. Exit is a trailing stop: for a long, stop_t = max(UpperBound_t, VWAP_t); for a short, stop_t = min(LowerBound_t, VWAP_t). The paper says 'as soon as the price crosses either the current band or the VWAP, the position is closed'. Anything still open is closed at 16:00. VWAP uses regular-session data only. There is no profit target. Sizing: shares = AUM x min(4, 2% / sigma_SPY,14d) / open. Companion paper (Zarattini & Aziz, SSRN 4416622, QQQ/TQQQ 5-min ORB, 2016-2023): it grid-tested profit targets of 1R-10R against an end-of-day exit, with stops set as a % of the 14-day ATR. The best average R came from no target (exit at the close) with a tight stop.

Flat at the close. Vol target 2% a day, leverage cap 4x. Commission $0.0035/share; a robustness run used the I-Star slippage model.

Stop at the opposite band: total 178%, 6.2%/yr, vol 10.9%, Sharpe 0.61, hit rate 54%, MDD 21%, worst day -10.3%, 5,494 trades. Stop = max(current band, VWAP): total 380%, 9.7%/yr, vol 7.7%, Sharpe 1.24, hit rate 43%, MDD 12%, worst day -4.8%, skew moves from -1.24 to +1.29, 7,668 trades. Adding vol-target sizing: 1,985%, 19.6%/yr, Sharpe 1.33, MDD 25% (Sharpe 1.17 under I-Star slippage). VWAP-only trail (Q22, data to Dec 2024): Sharpe 1.17 vs 1.35 for band + VWAP, MDD 27% vs 25%. Caveats: the authors sell trading education. A different paper by two of them uses VWAP as both entry and exit (claimed Sharpe 2.1); its QuantConnect replications were called 'very poor' and 'a lot less exciting' out of sample. A follow-up by Maroy (SSRN 5095349) reports Sharpe >3 for VWAP/ladder exits, but every parameter was optimised in-sample.

Real rows carry price, vwap, risk_pct and side, so stop = price x (1 -/+ risk_pct/100). Method on H.minute_data() cash candles: (1) VWAP_t = cumsum(typical price x volume) / cumsum(volume) from 09:15. (2) Enter at the open of the minute after the signal. (3) Each later minute: if the bar trades through the structural stop, exit at the stop (same gap handling as fills.simulate). If the 1-min close is below VWAP_t (above for a short), exit at the next minute's open. (4) Square off at 15:29. (5) Cost with costs.round_trip + costs.slippage(..., 0.02) on the same lots. So for v3 the VWAP trail starts near the structural stop and tightens as VWAP catches up, while a raw VWAP trail would cut many Fable-OP entries early. Limitation: no futures minute bars are cached; the real set has only per-policy outcomes in six/pull.json. After that it trails 1.0R behind the best price, moving in 0.5R increments. It was compared on identical entries and price paths against HOLD (stop only, held) and MECH1-3 (exit on the 1st, 2nd or 3rd consecutive opposite 5-minute candle). Kaminski & Lo (J. Financial Markets 2014): stop-loss rules add expected return only when returns are positively serially correlated (momentum); under a random walk they lower it. Chandelier exit (LeBeau): stop = highest high since entry - k x ATR; standard settings are 22 periods and k = 3 on daily bars.

After that, max(0, 0.5 x floor((MFE - 1.0) / 0.5)): MFE 1.5R puts the stop at +0.5R, 2.0R at +1.0R, 2.5R at +1.5R. No target; square off at 15:29. Declared settings: S1 as published.
