India VIX is not cached, but realized Nifty vol is Gao's own conditioning variable. For signal minute t on day d: RV(d,t) = sqrt(sum of (ln C_i / C_(i-1))^2) over Nifty 1-minute closes from 09:15 to t. rv_ratio = RV(d,t) / the mean of RV at the same clock minute over the previous 14 sessions (time-matched, like Zarattini's noise area). For signals before 09:25 (about 25% of rows have minutes_since_open <= 7), use the previous session's full-day RV ratio. Optional market-volume twin: total volume of the 218 stocks from 09:15 to t / the 14-day mean of the same window. Declared settings, design window only: S1 exit switch: s_opus_v3 >= 75, n = 6, policy CLOSE_TR when rv_ratio >= 1, else T1. S2 as S1 with the cut at the design-window 67th percentile. S3 filter: drop signals with rv_ratio below the design-window 33rd percentile (v3 exits at T1, Fable-OP at T3). S4 as S1 but switching on the market-volume ratio. Harness-ready: def spec(df): t = H.pick(df, 's_opus_v3', 75, 6); t['pol'] = np.where(t.rv_ratio >= cut, 'CLOSE_TR', 'T1'); return t. It uses the existing net_* columns, so the real set is judged on real futures prices. Volatility-scaled half sizing on quiet days is not feasible: 71% of unseen and 65% of known signals are a single lot, so half size becomes a skip.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial, in spirit only. Regime switches on the Nifty 20/50-day averages and the 20-day change (trend regimes) were tried, and Switch-1 is a trend-based exit switch. A volatility-based day regime or exit switch was not tried. It is not among the 22 COMMON features (nifty_chg is the raw move, not volatility).
pool.why_it_could_beat: Each exit wins on a different set: v3 at T1 is strong on real H1, while CLOSE and CLOSE_TR are strong on unseen and real H2. That points to a state-dependent exit. Theory and out-of-sample evidence say continuation into the close pays on high-vol days and fades on quiet ones. Switching to CLOSE_TR only when the market is moving abnormally, and banking T1 on quiet days, could keep v3's edge on the real set and recover the unseen loss.
pool.risks: Gao's result is for the index's last half-hour, not stock breakouts. Volatility clusters, so the switch may stay on or off for weeks. The cut is fixed on about 78 design days. Signals in the first few minutes have only a short window.

pool.name: Prior-day range-compression filter: NR4/NR7/triangle bonus, and no momentum trade after a prior trend day
pool.published_rules: Zarattini et al. (Table 5) classify each day by the previous day's daily-bar pattern and compare the next day's P&L of the intraday momentum strategy. Patterns: NR4 (range smallest of the last 4 days); NR7 (smallest of 7); ID, inside day; OD, outside day; Triangle (high below the highs of the previous 2 days and low above their lows); Trend day (open below the 15th percentile of the range and close above the 85th, or the reverse, with range above the 14-day average range); Big Tail (open and close both in the top 25% of the range, or the reverse); Strong/Weak closure (close above the 90th or below the 10th percentile of the range). The authors suggest larger bets after NR4, NR7 and Triangle days.
pool.published_params: NR4; NR7; triangle with a 2-day lookback; trend day at the 15/85 percentiles with range above the 14-day mean range.
pool.claimed_performance: SPY 2007-2024, index-level, in-sample. Next-day average P&L / t-stat / hit rate / Sharpe: unconditional 2,620 days, 12 bps, t 5.34, 43%, Sharpe 1.7. NR4 660 days, 22 bps, t 5.14, 45%, Sharpe 3.2. NR7 367 days, 16 bps, t 3.07, Sharpe 2.5. Triangle 664 days, 14 bps, t 3.19, Sharpe 2.0. ID 260 days, 5 bps, t 0.85, Sharpe 0.8. OD 260 days, 7 bps, Sharpe 1.0. Trend day 215 days, -2 bps, t -0.24, Sharpe -0.3. Big tail 85 days, 19 bps, t 1.17, Sharpe 2.0. Strong/weak close 422 days, 14 bps, t 2.04, Sharpe 1.6.
pool.our_data_mapping: Build per-stock flags from the H.minute_data() daily candles (available from Jan 2024), using only rows dated before the signal day. Flags: NR4 and NR7 on (high - low); inside day; triangle; and a prior-day trend day in the trade's direction (long: open_(d-1) <= low + 0.15 x range, close >= low + 0.85 x range, range > mean 14-day range; mirror for shorts). Build the same flags for Nifty from v2/data/nifty_daily.json. Declared settings: S1 add 10 to the score if the stock is NR4, NR7 or triangle (lets marginal signals cross 75). S2 drop signals whose stock had a same-direction trend day yesterday. S3 S1 applied at Nifty level (whole day). S4 S1 + S2. Exits are unchanged (v3 at T1, Fable-OP at T3), so the harness net_* columns apply on all sets, including real futures. The 6-slot cap binds: on real, 521 v3 signals score >= 75 but 335 are taken (4.1 qualifying a day; slots go by time). So a penalty or bonus changes which trades fill the slots.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None found. No prior-day range-pattern feature exists; range_atr is today's range and is REAL_ONLY. Loosely related to Fable-OP's 'move today in daily ATRs'.
pool.why_it_could_beat: Breakouts from a compressed range have more room before the stock reaches its typical daily range. After a full trend day, momentum the next day fails: -2 bps and Sharpe -0.3 on SPY. Penalising post-trend-day breakouts and favouring post-compression ones is a pre-open stock filter with no look-ahead, and no current score uses it.
pool.risks: The only evidence is index-level and in-sample. NR7 is rare (about one day in seven per stock), so S1 adds few trades. Daily-pattern effects may differ for individual Indian stocks. Each set has only about 130 days.

pool.name: Nifty RSI(5) as a dealer-gamma proxy: trade momentum harder after short-term index declines
pool.published_rules: Zarattini et al. (section 4.5) regress the strategy's daily return in bps on SPY's 5-day RSI at the previous close: Ret_t = alpha + beta x RSI5_(t-1). The rationale comes from Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (JFE 2021): when option dealers are net short gamma, their delta hedging trades with the move and amplifies intraday trends. After market declines dealers are more likely to be short gamma; after rallies, long gamma, which brings mean reversion.
pool.published_params: RSI period 5 on daily closes, taken at the previous close.
pool.claimed_performance: SPY 2007-2024: beta = -3.25 bps per RSI point, p = 0.001 (lower RSI means higher intraday-momentum P&L). Baltussen et al.: market intraday momentum across 60+ futures, 1974-2020. In the S&P 500 it is present when net gamma exposure is negative and stronger the more negative it is. No Indian market is in their sample; I checked the futures list.
pool.our_data_mapping: Compute RSI5 (Wilder) from Nifty daily closes in v2/data/nifty_daily.json, the file H.regime() uses, taking the value at d-1. Declared settings: S1 exit switch: v3 >= 75, policy CLOSE_TR when RSI5_(d-1) < 50, else T1. S2 skip days with RSI5_(d-1) above the design-window 80th percentile. S3 Fable-OP at T3 on days with RSI5 < 50, v3 at T1 otherwise. S4 as S1 with the cut at the design-window median. Everything uses harness columns; no minute data is needed. The real driver, dealer gamma from option-chain open interest, cannot be computed because option-chain history is not cached.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial. Regime switches on the Nifty 20/50-day averages and on the 20-day change were tried, as was Switch-1 (downtrend days use v3 at T1). RSI5 is a one-week state. Zarattini's sign implies the opposite exit choice to Switch-1 after declines: hold longer rather than take T1. RSI5 is correlated with r20, so check that it adds anything.
pool.why_it_could_beat: If Indian option sellers hedge the way US dealers do, intraday trends should persist after short index sell-offs and mean-revert after rallies. A single pre-open number used as a switch is hard to overfit.
pool.risks: India's option market is structured differently (retail buyers, prop sellers, weekly Tuesday expiry), which could flip or erase the gamma mechanism. It overlaps with trend gates that already failed. About 130 days per set give few independent regimes.

pool.name: Daily loss limit: no new entries after 2 stop-outs or after -2R realized in the day
pool.published_rules: Practitioner rule: stop opening trades for the session after a set number of losses or a set loss amount. The only opened source with numbers is an MNQ ORB test in backtesting.py. It stops trading after one losing trade per session, treated as a fixed constraint. Its other rules: stop at the opposite side of the opening range, an R-multiple target, and an SMA(200) direction filter. Practitioner guides I saw only in search snippets suggest a daily stop of about 2-3x the per-trade risk, with a loss counter that resets each day; I did not open them.
pool.published_params: One losing trade per session (opened source).
pool.claimed_performance: MNQ ORB with the one-loss rule. In-sample Feb 2020 to Dec 2022: 451 trades, win rate 30.4%, profit factor 1.43, Sharpe 1.37, MDD -10.9%. Out-of-sample Jan 2023 to Feb 2026: 474 trades, win rate 24.9%, profit factor 1.32, Sharpe 1.10, MDD -12.8%. No comparison with and without the rule is published, and I found no controlled study of intraday loss limits.
pool.our_data_mapping: Needs exit timestamps, which the harness does not have. Re-simulate each signal with scanner.equity.fills.simulate on cash minutes to get its exit time under the chosen policy (T1 for v3, T3 for Fable-OP). P&L still comes from the harness net_* columns, which are real futures for the real set; using cash candles only for timing is a reasonable stand-in. Then, per day and in time order under the live rule, skip every signal whose entry minute falls after the trigger. Declared settings: S1 trigger = 2 trades closed at their original stop. S2 trigger = realized day P&L <= -Rs 30,000 (2R). S3 as S1 but block only the side that was stopped. S4 max 4 trades a day instead of 6.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None; the max-6 rule is the only cap in use.
pool.why_it_could_beat: The bar also requires worst day and max drawdown within 1.25x the better baseline. Opus v3's unseen worst day is -57,143, about 3.8R. Same-day breakouts share the market factor (about 4 qualifying signals a day), so failures cluster on choppy or reversal days. If stop-outs are positively correlated within a day, cutting those days short improves the worst day and drawdown at little cost. That could let a more aggressive exit (the VWAP trail, stepped trail or Nifty-volatility candidates) pass the risk part of the bar.
pool.risks: The evidence is anecdotal. If trade outcomes are not correlated within a day, the rule only removes trades and net profit falls. It can cut off afternoon recovery trades. Re-simulating exit times on cash candles adds approximation.

pool.name: Constant-delta strike: re-solve the strike per signal for |delta| about 0.65 from its IV and days to expiry, instead of a fixed % in the money
pool.published_rules: Zerodha Varsity Module 5 ch.22 'Re-introducing call & put options' (rules for BUYING; the series is split into halves of about 15 days). 1st half: target in 5 days -> about 2 strikes OTM ('I would suggest you buy 2 or 3 strikes away from ATM and not beyond that'); 15 days -> ATM or 1 strike OTM ('I would not recommend buying options that are more than 1 strike away from ATM'); 25 days -> slightly ITM ('One should certainly avoid buying ATM or OTM options'); target on expiry day -> ITM ('all strikes except ITM tend to lose money'). 2nd half (theta stronger): target the same day -> 2-3 strikes OTM (ITM/ATM 'not worth buying'); 5 days -> 1 strike OTM; 10 days -> slightly ITM or ATM; expiry day -> ITM. The worked example assumes spot 5000 and a 4 % move to 5200. QuantInsti intraday guide: scalping uses 'at-the-money (ATM) or slightly in-the-money (ITM)' options; breakouts favour 'short-dated options with a high delta'; avoid low delta (for example 0.05). AlgoTest: 'closer to expiry, Theta eats into OTM premiums fast, so ATM or ITM strikes tend to hold up better'; a conservative trade means ITM 'for higher Delta'. QuantInsti EPAT index-momentum project (Nifty, 2007-2017): 'ATM Strike Prices are observed to give best results' (compared with OTM).
pool.published_params: Varsity: strike distance chosen by time to target and by series half (2-3 strikes OTM ... slightly ITM). Proposed settings, declared in advance: target |delta| 0.55 / 0.65 / 0.75; pick one on the design window.
pool.claimed_performance: Varsity gives charts of modelled premiums only, no P&L figures. In those charts, far OTM wins only for a large (4 %) move that arrives quickly; near expiry, slow targets favour ITM. EPAT (index options, multi-day holds, 1 Jan 2007-30 Nov 2017, parameters optimised on 2007-2015 and validated on 2016-Nov 2017): about 600 % over about 10 years, 119 trades; CALLs INR 4,57,651 vs PUTs INR 1,67,372; ATM beat OTM. In-house context, not published: the lead's grid (_mine/optgrid.log) shows fixed 2 % ITM > 1 % > ATM on the design window for v3 (T3: 3,93,914 vs 3,51,296).
pool.our_data_mapping: option_net() broadcasts strike_pct per row (K = F0*(1 -/+ strike_pct/100)), so pass an array. z = scipy.stats.norm.ppf(delta); T0 = H._years(t.o_entry_ts, t.o_expiry); v = t.o_iv.values*np.sqrt(T0); call = t.o_kind.eq('CE').values; k = np.where(call, 100*(1-np.exp(-(z*v-0.5*v*v))), 100*(np.exp(z*v+0.5*v*v)-1)); pnl = H.option_net(t, pol, strike_pct=k). For delta 0.65 (z=0.385) and the median IV 0.29: about 2.4 % ITM at 21 days to expiry and about 1.3 % ITM at 6 days. Optional: round k to the stock's strike grid. Strike intervals are not cached, but the 280-signal real legs (options/legs_iv.pkl, column strike) show them for the symbols traded in Oct-Nov. Wrap it as a spec function that returns trades with their own 'pnl' column; report option_net(..., detail=True).outlay. To stay outside the lead's plain grid, combine it with a new selection rule (for example the pace filter or equal-risk sizing below).
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial overlap. The lead's grid tests FIXED strike_pct -1/0/+1/+2 % on the baselines' own picks. A constant-delta strike varies from 1 % to 4 % ITM with IV and days to expiry, which is a different rule. Do not submit it alone on the baseline picks.
pool.why_it_could_beat: T1 is only 0.3-0.9 daily ATR away, so the option P&L is dominated by delta times the move and the gamma convexity is small. Higher delta captures more of the futures edge, which is why the grid favours ITM. A fixed 2 % ITM strike is deep (delta about 0.8) at 6 days to expiry and shallow (about 0.6) on high-IV names at 35 days. Holding delta constant evens out each trade's exposure and avoids paying ITM spreads where they buy nothing.
pool.risks: The model has no skew. Real ITM calls (strike below spot) carry higher IV than ATM, so the modelled ITM-call gain is overstated; ITM puts are slightly understated. ITM stock options are less liquid, with wider rupee spreads, and slip is fixed at 0.25 %. Part of the ITM 'edge' is plain extra delta at the same lots, i.e. leverage. Also run it at equal delta exposure (lots_mult = 0.5/delta) to separate edge from leverage, and check that worst day stays within 1.25x.

pool.name: Days-to-expiry expiry switch: next month only in the second half of the series, and only for slow trades, with a stressed next-month spread
pool.published_rules: Varsity theta chapter: 'when there were 20 days to expiry the option was trading around 150, but when we approach towards expiry the drop in premium seems to accelerate (option value drops below 50)'. The author (comment reply, Nov 2022) says buying 'its best if done in the first half'. Varsity ch.22: decay is stronger in the 2nd half (day 15 to expiry). QuantInsti EPAT: choose the current or the near-month contract by a days-to-expiry threshold, optimised at 20 days. Zerodha physical-settlement policy for long ITM stock options: delivery margin from E-4 (10 % of VaR+ELM+adhoc), E-3 25 %, E-2 45 %, E-1 25 % of contract value, expiry day 50 % of contract value; fresh long OTM current-month positions are blocked on E-1 and E. Substack (opinion, no data): the next-month stock option series 'has near zero volume until front-month expiry approaches'.
pool.published_params: Varsity: halves of about 15 days. EPAT: 20-day threshold. Exchange: delivery margin from E-4. Proposed settings: switch when calendar days to expiry <= 10 / 14 / 18, with the next-month slip at 1.0 % (stress) as well as the model's 0.25 %.
pool.claimed_performance: No intraday-specific numbers. Varsity's illustration: premium falls from about 150 at 20 days to expiry to below 50 near expiry. EPAT overall: about 600 % over 10 years, 119 trades (index options, multi-day holds).
pool.our_data_mapping: dte = (pd.to_datetime(t.o_expiry)-pd.to_datetime(t.day)).dt.days.values (the cached range is 6-40, median 21; o_expiry already rolls at <= 4 sessions). a = H.option_net(t, pol); b = H.option_net(t, pol, expiry='next', slip_pct=1.0); pnl = np.where(dte <= D, b, a). Hybrid (recommended): next month only when dte <= D AND the pace/break-even ratio of the next candidate is below its threshold (a slow trade); otherwise use the standard contract. Report outlay with detail=True.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Partial overlap. The lead's grid runs std vs next for ALL rows of the baselines. A conditional switch by days to expiry and/or trade speed is new.
pool.why_it_could_beat: Theory cuts both ways for intraday holds. For an ATM option with constant IV, gamma and theta both scale as 1/sqrt(T), so the break-even move over a hold of h is R/F = IV*sqrt(h) whatever the days to expiry. Shorter-dated options amplify both the convexity gain and the decay. Trades that exit at the stop or target with |move| = R greater than the implied move over the hold do better in the near contract. Slow trades that drift to the 15:29 square-off with small moves do better in the next month (less theta, and vega is larger but IV is held constant). Switching only the slow, late-series trades keeps the gamma of the fast ones.
pool.risks: The multi-day evidence (Varsity, EPAT) may not carry over to 1-3 hour holds. Next-month stock options are much less liquid, and the model's 0.25 % slip understates their cost, so judge only on the 1.0 % stressed run. Larger vega for the next month means more exposure to IV moves the model cannot see.

pool.name: Intraday realised-vs-implied pace filter: buy the option only when today's minute-level realised vol exceeds the option's IV (the Goyal-Saretto HV-IV logic moved intraday)
pool.published_rules: Goyal & Saretto (JFE 2009): sort stocks on the 'difference between historical realized volatility and at-the-money implied volatility'. A zero-cost strategy goes long options (straddles / delta-hedged calls) on the portfolio with a large positive gap and short those with a large negative gap, held about a month. Muravyev & Ni (JFE 2020), via the CXO summary: delta-hedged options lose overnight and gain intraday, because option prices ignore that stock volatility is much higher intraday. Macroption: period sigma = IV x sqrt(period / periods per year); daily = IV / sqrt(252). Quantsapp: adjust premium stops and targets for the theta of the intended hold.
pool.published_params: Goyal-Saretto: decile sorts on HV(12m) - IV, monthly rebalance. Proposed settings: RV_today/IV >= 1.0 / 1.25 / 1.5, picked on the design window.
pool.claimed_performance: Goyal-Saretto abstract: an 'economically and statistically significant average monthly return', robust across market conditions, risk characteristics, industries and option-liquidity measures, and not explained by standard risk factors. The decile figures sit behind the paywall; I could not open them. Muravyev-Ni (Jan 2004-Apr 2013, gross, midquotes): S&P 500 delta-hedged -0.7 %/day = -1.0 % overnight + 0.3 % intraday. Single-stock options: -0.4 % overnight, +0.1 % intraday. Costs: spreads swamp the overnight trade for most investors.
pool.our_data_mapping: mins, daily, nifty, lot = H.minute_data() (load once). For each signal: r = log returns of the cash 1-minute closes from 09:16 up to and including the signal minute (drop the opening gap); RV_today = r.std()*sqrt(375*252); ratio = RV_today / t.o_iv. Rule: baseline score >= 75 AND ratio >= c; then the first 6 per day in time order (pick() after masking the score to NaN). A no-minute-data variant is the analytic gamma-theta break-even. With K = F0, s = o_iv, T0 = H._years(o_entry_ts, o_expiry), R = o_risk_abs, sgn = +1 for CE / -1 for PE, and h = the design-window median minutes to exit for the chosen policy (a constant): pT = H._b76(F0+sgn*R, K, T0-H.DECAY*h/525600, s, call), pS = H._b76(F0-sgn*R, K, ..., s, call), p0 = H._b76(F0, K, T0, s, call). Gain G = q*(pT-p0) - H.opt_costs(p0, pT, q); loss L = q*(p0-pS) + H.opt_costs(p0, pS, q); take rows with G/L >= 1. This is equivalent to R/F >= IV*sqrt(h)-type break-even plus costs.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Overlaps in spirit with Fable-OP's 'move today in ATRs' and 'early in session' parts and with the v3 rel_vol gate. Our IV is a function of ATR, so the break-even variant is close to a stop_atr floor. That was tried only as a STOP change (0.4-0.7 ATR floor), never as a filter. Minute-return RV/IV has not been tried.
pool.why_it_could_beat: A bought option is long gamma. It earns when realised movement during the hold beats the IV paid, and intraday realised vol clusters strongly. Selecting signals whose stock is already moving rough and fast relative to its IV targets the trades where convexity outruns decay. The same signal on a sleepy tape, which drifts to the 15:29 close, is where options bleed relative to futures.
pool.risks: Model IV is ATR-based and fixed, so the 'IV cheap' channel is invisible. Only the effect through the futures path is measured, and a real benefit would be larger only if real IV lags realised vol. High intraday RV names may have IV already marked up live (which the model cannot see). It may concentrate trades in the first 30 minutes, where option spreads are widest (see the time-of-day candidate).

pool.name: Equal option-risk lot sizing at the baseline's capital: size each trade so the modelled option loss at the futures stop is the same, with a 20 % pad, a lot cap and the same median premium outlay
pool.published_rules: Tradefundrr: 'Stop distance on the underlying x option delta x 100 = estimated loss per contract'; pad it for time decay, falling IV and the spread, planning as if the loss could be about 20 % higher than the delta estimate (more on very short-dated options); 'Divide planned risk by the backstop loss per contract'. It recommends a hybrid for directional option trades: the exit decision on the underlying level, plus a premium backstop as a hard ceiling. Quantsapp: 'If the volatility-based stop is too wide for your risk budget, reduce the position size rather than tightening the stop'; theta-adjust premium levels for the intended hold (example: a Rs 50 option, stop 45 / target 60 becomes about 41 / 56 for an open-to-close hold at 7 days to expiry). QuantInsti EPAT: lots = floor((balance x 15 % / option price) / lot size).
pool.published_params: Pad 20 %. EPAT 15 % of balance per trade. Proposed settings: budget B = B_eq (set on the design window so that the median premium outlay equals the baseline's, about Rs 20,300 ATM), Rs 10,000, Rs 15,000; lot cap 3x the futures lots.
pool.claimed_performance: No empirical stop/sizing performance is published; the Tradefundrr numbers are illustrative ($2 x 0.50 x 100 = about $100 per contract; with a $1,000 daily limit and a $150 backstop, 5 contracts risk $750). EPAT (which sizes on premium): about 600 % over 10 years on Nifty options.
pool.our_data_mapping: p0 = H._b76(F0, K, T0, iv, call); pS = H._b76(F0 - sgn*o_risk_abs, K, T0 - H.DECAY*hS/525600, iv, call), where hS = design-window median minutes to stop for that policy (a constant). Per-unit loss Lu = 1.2*(p0-pS) + H.opt_costs(p0, pS, 1). lots = clip(floor(B/(Lu*lot)), 1, 3*fut_lots); pnl = H.option_net(t, pol, qty=lots*lot, detail=True) for net and outlay. Lot size: unseen/known have 'lot' and 'lots' columns; for real rows map lot by symbol and month from the known set (same dates), or fut_lots = o_qty/lot. Report premium outlay per trade, worst day and max DD separately, as rule 5 requires.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None. The brief lists lot count as an open option lever.
pool.why_it_could_beat: Futures sizing equalises the FUTURES loss at the stop, but the option loss at that stop is (Delta*R - 0.5*Gamma*R^2 + theta*h)/R of it. That ratio is large for tight stops, high IV and short R, and small for wide stops where convexity cushions the loss. Equalising the option risk at the same median capital moves lots from trades where the option is all theta-and-spread drag to trades where the option's asymmetry (capped loss, convex gain) is real. This is a reallocation, not added leverage, when B = B_eq.
pool.risks: With B = Rs 15,000 it is roughly 2x leverage for ATM, which will likely break the 1.25x worst-day bar; report it only as a separate variant. A large lot count in thin stock options raises real slippage beyond the model's 0.25 %. The pad and hS are assumptions. A gap or IV collapse can make the realised loss exceed the modelled one.

pool.name: Option-aware time of day: charge a realistic opening spread (skip or demand a higher score before about 09:45), let calls run into the afternoon, book puts early
pool.published_rules: Chan, Chung & Johnson (JFQA 1995): stock spreads are U-shaped, but CBOE option spreads show 'a very different intraday pattern - one that declines sharply after the open, and then levels off'. U. Saskatchewan thesis (CBOE equity options, 2010): an 'L-shaped spread pattern', high in the morning and stable only 'after the first 90 minutes of trading'; option depth is reverse-U. Muravyev & Ni (JFE 2020, CXO summary): intraday delta-hedged option returns are positive, and 'the positive intraday return concentrates in the afternoon, especially near the close'. Bhat, Pandey & Nageswara Rao (J. Futures Markets 2024, Nifty options 2017-2020): short option positions gain overnight and lose intraday; 'average postnoon returns are significantly negative (positive) for short positions in call (put) options, while prenoon returns are largely insignificant'. So post-noon, long calls gain and long puts lose. 'The return asymmetry declines with increase in option moneyness and maturity', and is weaker on jump days.
pool.published_params: Opening window about 90 min (US options); post-noon split (Nifty). Proposed settings: (a) early cut 15 or 30 minutes after open, with early slip 0.75 % or 1.0 %; (b) LONG exit T3 or CLOSE_TR crossed with SHORT exit T1 or T2. At most 4 combinations are picked on the design window.
pool.claimed_performance: Muravyev-Ni (gross, midquotes): S&P options +0.3 %/day intraday vs -1.0 % overnight; equity options +0.1 % vs -0.4 %; OTM +0.03 % intraday vs -1.7 % overnight; ITM +0.07 % vs -0.2 %; under 3 weeks to expiry +0.07 % vs -2.6 %. Bhat et al.: profitable before costs, not after; no magnitudes on the pages I could open. Our own data (not published): in the 280 real option legs (21 Oct-13 Nov 2026), entries at or before 09:30 had a stale option price in 11.4 % of cases (n=176) vs 0 % for 10:00-12:00 (n=42).
pool.our_data_mapping: (a) Cost realism: slip = np.where(t.minutes_since_open < cut, 0.75, 0.25); pnl = H.option_net(t, pol, slip_pct=slip). Rule: entries with minutes_since_open < cut need score >= 85 (others >= 75), then the first 6 per day. Note the median signal comes 29-31 minutes after the open, so half the signals sit in this window. (b) Side-specific exit: a spec function t = H.pick(df, score, 75); t['pol'] = np.where(t.side == 'LONG', 'T3', 'T1') (or CLOSE_TR / T2); run() then reads opt_<pol> per row. Validate the mechanism with the real legs (options/legs_iv.pkl has o_exit and the modelled pred_exit): residual o_exit - pred_exit by side x exit hour (before/after 12:00).
pool.already_tried_overlap: Fable-OP rewards 'early in session' (15 points), the opposite direction for options. v2 split SCORING by side, and Switch-1 switches policy by REGIME. An exit-policy split by side, and opening-spread-aware entry, are not on the tried list.
pool.why_it_could_beat: For a bought option the early entries pay the widest option spreads of the day, and the model charges a flat 0.25 %. The afternoon is when long-option (delta-hedged) returns are positive in US data, and for long calls in Nifty data, while long puts lose post-noon. Keeping calls on through the afternoon and taking puts off quickly lines the holding time up with where the option premium has historically been fair or cheap.
pool.risks: The harness has no intraday IV pattern (constant IV, uniform decay of 2.31x calendar), so (b) can show only its futures-path effect; the option-specific gain needs real quotes. The evidence comes from index options (Nifty, S&P), not NSE single stocks. Skipping early signals cuts the most profitable futures window. The real-leg sample is one expiry and 280 signals.

pool.name: Spot-vol (vega) side filter: calls only on stock-specific breakouts, puts preferred on market-driven breakdowns
pool.published_rules: Dennis, Mayhew & Stivers (JFQA 2006): daily stock returns are substantially negatively related to innovations in SYSTEMATIC (index) implied volatility and nearly unrelated to innovations in IDIOSYNCRATIC implied volatility; 'asymmetric volatility is primarily attributed to systematic market-wide factors'; IV innovations proxy well for expected-volatility innovations. Varsity ch.22: 'Regardless of time to expiry, the premium always increases with increase in volatility'; buy when volatility is expected to rise and avoid buying when it is expected to fall.
pool.published_params: Proposed settings: LONG (call) allowed only if nifty_chg <= +0.3 % (or +0.6 %) at the signal minute; SHORT (put) requires nifty_chg <= -0.5 % (or -0.8 %), where setup B already needs <= -0.25 %.
pool.claimed_performance: No trading P&L published; the result is a regression relation (daily data). No magnitudes on the abstract page I could open.
pool.our_data_mapping: Features nifty_chg (raw), day_chg (direction-adjusted), side. Rule: mask the baseline score where (LONG & nifty_chg > cap) or (SHORT & nifty_chg > floor), then pick(). Optional rank for longs: idiosyncratic move = day_chg - nifty_chg. The harness prices entry and exit with ONE sigma (option_net uses s for p0 and p1), so the vega channel is invisible. To see it, reprice p1 yourself with H._b76 and sigma1 = sigma0*(1 - b*r_nifty_during_hold), using Nifty minutes from H.minute_data(). The coefficient b can only be estimated from the 280 real legs (Oct-Nov 2026, inside the test window), so use it for model checking, not selection.
pool.already_tried_overlap: Fable-OP's 'stock moving without the index' (15 points) is applied to both sides alike. Setup B needs Nifty down >= 0.25 %. Regime switches by Nifty trend were tried. The side-asymmetric option version (calls idiosyncratic, puts systematic) is new.
pool.why_it_could_beat: A call bought because the whole market is rallying loses vega as index IV falls with the rally. A call on a stock breaking out alone keeps its IV. A put bought into a market sell-off gains vega as systematic IV rises. The futures result is the same, but the option result differs by the vega P&L, which the scanner's ATM monthly options carry (vega is not small at 20 or more days to expiry).
pool.risks: Needs real IV to verify, and the model cannot reward it. Calls on stock-specific moves may face their own IV crush on news days. Tightening the put filter cuts trades on mild down days.

pool.name: Skip option buys when IV is likely rich: results-day filter and previous-day IV/RV rank (route those signals to futures or skip them)
pool.published_rules: Jain, Varma & Agarwalla (J. Futures Markets 2018), per Prof. Varma's blog: implied volatility of Indian single-stock options 'consistently exceeds realized volatility by too large an amount to be easily explained as a rational risk premium'; the premium 'appears to be higher than in other markets'; single-stock IV has 'a strong systematic component responding to changes in market wide risk aversion'; IV has incremental predictive power for future volatility. Saurav, Agarwalla & Varma (American Business Review 2024; IIMA page): in Indian stock options, IV and skew 'rise monotonically before the EA day' and fall after it; one day before, skew and the put/call volume ratio predict the sign of the surprise. Goyal & Saretto: buy options where HV - IV is large positive, avoid or sell where it is large negative. Cao & Han (JFE 2013, CXO summary): delta-hedged returns are far more negative on high-volatility stocks; long low-vol / short high-vol ATM calls make about 2 %/month at midquotes, and paying 50-100 % of the closing spread cuts the about 1 %/month edge to about zero.
pool.published_params: Proposed settings: (i) no option buy on a results day when results come during market hours; (ii) no option buy when the previous day's ATM IV / 20-day close-to-close RV is in the top tercile of the F&O universe that day.
pool.claimed_performance: Cao-Han: about 2 %/month (Jan 1996-Oct 2009, midquotes), with frictions about 0. Goyal-Saretto: significant monthly returns (figures not on the abstract page). Jain-Varma-Agarwalla and Saurav et al.: no P&L figures on the pages I could open.
pool.our_data_mapping: Not cached. Needs (1) results / board-meeting dates per symbol (NSE corporate announcements) and (2) daily option settlement prices per strike and expiry (NSE F&O bhavcopy, public daily files), from which previous-day ATM IV per stock is backed out with H._b76. That gives a no-look-ahead IV/RV rank and a real IV per trade to feed option_net(iv_mult = IV_real/o_iv). A weak proxy is possible now: skip when |gap| > 1 ATR or the prior day's range > 2 ATR (IV usually marked up after shocks), but the harness's ATR-based IV would not register any option-specific gain.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None.
pool.why_it_could_beat: The scanner buys whatever is breaking out, including stocks around results, where IV is at its peak or about to collapse. An intraday holder caught in a mid-session results release loses vega on a winning direction call. Indian single-stock IV carries an unusually large premium over realised vol, and routing the IV-richest names to futures (or skipping them) avoids the worst-priced options.
pool.risks: The data must be built first. Results timing (pre-market, intraday or after the close) matters and must be known in advance. The IV/RV rank is daily, while the edge is intraday. Thinner trade counts.

pool.name: Option-liquidity screen with tiered slippage: trade options only on liquid underlyings (cash-turnover proxy), checked against stale real option prints
pool.published_rules: Christoffersen, Goyenko, Jacobs & Karoui (RFS 2018): using intraday effective spreads, 'the risk-adjusted return spread for illiquid over liquid equity options is 3.4 % per day for at-the-money calls and 2.5 % for at-the-money puts'; attributed to US market makers' net long inventory. Cao-Han (CXO): paying 50-100 % of the closing spread removes an about 1 %/month option edge. QuantInsti: 'check the bid-ask spread and ensure the option has enough liquidity'; 'Opt for options with higher volume and open interest'; use limit orders. Substack (opinion, no data): NSE current-month single-stock option spreads 'can go to 10-100%'; the next-month series has 'near zero volume'.
pool.published_params: Proposed settings: liquidity tiers fixed in advance by the 20-day average cash turnover rank: top 60 -> slip 0.25 %, 61-120 -> 0.6 %, rest -> 1.2 %. Option trades only in the top N, N = 80 or 120.
pool.claimed_performance: Christoffersen et al.: 3.4 %/day (calls) and 2.5 %/day (puts) illiquid-minus-liquid, risk-adjusted (US). Cao-Han: about 1 %/month edge goes to about 0 after paying 50-100 % of the spread. Our real legs: stale entry prints are concentrated at the open (11.4 % at or before 09:30, n=176, vs 0 % 10:00-12:00, n=42).
pool.our_data_mapping: From H.minute_data(): per symbol and day, turnover = sum(close*volume) over the session; ADV20 = mean of the previous 20 sessions (shift by 1 day, no look-ahead); rank across symbols per day. slip = tier lookup; pnl = H.option_net(t, pol, slip_pct=slip) (opt_costs takes a per-row slip). Filter: mask scores of rows with rank > N, then pick() (the max-6 rule refills with later signals). Validate the proxy on options/legs_iv.pkl: the share of stale > 0 and the gap between o_entry and the modelled entry, by ADV tier.
pool.already_tried_overlap: None. No liquidity gate or per-symbol option cost has been tested; the model charges 0.25 % to every name.
pool.why_it_could_beat: The modelled option edge assumes 0.25 % slippage on every name. On thin stock options the real round trip can cost several times that, turning small T1 wins into losses. Restricting to liquid names (or at least charging them honestly) keeps the trades whose option edge survives real spreads. That is what the option P&L the client actually books depends on.
pool.risks: Cash turnover is only a proxy for option liquidity. Tier thresholds are guesses until checked against real quotes. It may cut good trades in mid-caps that move well. Real option spreads also vary with time of day and moneyness, which a per-symbol tier ignores.

tests.name: VWAP trailing exit with no target, flat at 15:29 (noise-area paper's trail, cut down to the VWAP leg), on Fable-OP picks
tests.hypothesis: A bought option has a convex payoff, so it gains most from letting trend-day winners run and from cutting non-performers before the structural stop. Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon's VWAP trail with no target halved the worst day and doubled Sharpe against a loose fixed stop (SPY, in sample), and the ORB papers find exit-at-close beats every fixed R target. Replacing Fable-OP's fixed T3 with a VWAP trail should lift option net by keeping the right tail and trimming afternoon give-backs and slow losers.
tests.exact_rules: Picks: t = H.pick(df, S, 75, 6) with S = 's_fable_op' (S1-S3) or 's_opus_v3' (S4). Data: mins, daily, nifty, lot = H.minute_data(), loaded once per process; cash minutes of t.symbol on t.day. sgn = +1 LONG, -1 SHORT. Entry minute e = the bar after the signal bar (signal bar = column 'time'), E = open of bar e. Structural stop in cash: unseen/known use column 'stop'; real uses stop_c = E*(1 - sgn*o_risk_abs/o_F0). R = |E - stop_c|. Session VWAP_k = cumsum(((H+L+C)/3)*V)/cumsum(V) over bars 09:15..k (cash, regular session only). Walk bars k = e, e+1, ...: (1) Stop first: if a long bar's low <= stop_c (short: high >= stop_c), exit at stop_c, or at the bar's open if it opens beyond the stop. Gap handling is copied from scanner.equity.fills.simulate. (2) VWAP rule, only at the CHECK bars and only if not stopped in that bar: if a long's close < VWAP_k (short's close > VWAP_k), exit at the open of bar k+1. (3) Anything still open is squared off at 15:29 exactly as fills.simulate does for the CLOSE policy. No profit target. Option leg: set t['o_F1_VW'] = o_F0 * (X/E), where X is the cash exit price (this maps the cash move onto the scanner's underlying; exact on unseen/known, approximate on real), and t['o_exit_ts_VW'] = the exit bar timestamp in the same ISO +05:30 format as o_exit_ts_*. Then pnl = H.option_net(t, 'VW'), which applies the harness's 1-minute exit lag. Futures (reference): unseen/known lots*lot*sgn*(X-E) minus scanner.equity.costs.round_trip and costs.slippage(..., 0.02). Real: sgn*(X/E-1)*o_F0*o_qty minus the same costs. ENGINE CHECK, mandatory and reported before any VW result: with the VWAP rule disabled the engine must reproduce the harness CLOSE policy (o_F1_CLOSE, o_exit_ts_CLOSE, opt_CLOSE) on unseen/known within rounding. Also report the engine's own CLOSE and T3/T1 re-sim on real, so that engine differences are not counted as exit gains.
tests.fixed_params: VWAP from regular-session 1-minute data, recomputed every minute (paper). No profit target; flat at the close (both papers). Check grid every 30 minutes, as in the paper's HH:00/HH:30 checks (NSE opens 09:15, so checks are at the closes of the bars stamped 09:44, 10:14, ..., 15:14). The scanner's structural stop, entry at the next minute's open, Rs 15,000 futures-risk lots, max 6 a day and option costs/slippage as in the harness are kept unchanged. The paper's band leg (max(UpperBound, VWAP)) is dropped because scanner entries are not noise-band breaks, so most would exit at once.
tests.grid: S1: s_fable_op>=75 picks, VWAP checked at the 30-minute marks only (bars 09:44, 10:14, ..., 15:14), active from entry. S2: s_fable_op>=75, VWAP checked at every 1-minute close from the entry bar. S3: s_fable_op>=75, 1-minute checks, active only once MFE >= +0.5R (MFE from bar highs/lows since entry, in R). S4: s_opus_v3>=75 picks, as S1. Choose on the real design window (12 May-31 Aug, cash re-sim of the real picks): highest option net among the settings whose design option worst day and max DD are no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline; if none qualifies, take the highest net and flag it.
tests.exit_policy: New per-row policy 'VW': structural stop always live, plus a VWAP trail (exit at the next bar's open after a check-bar close beyond VWAP against the trade), no target, square-off at 15:29. The option is sold at the open of the minute after the futures exit (harness exit_lag_min = 1).
tests.selection: Live rule unchanged: per day in time order (ties by higher score, then symbol), the first 6 rows with s_fable_op >= 75 (S1-S3) or s_opus_v3 >= 75 (S4).
tests.compare_on: Clean like-for-like on unseen (bar set) and known (cash stand-in; the engine reproduces the harness CLOSE policy there). On real, and so on real 2nd half (bar set), it is a cash re-sim of the real picks mapped onto o_F0. That matches how the harness itself already times real-set exits from a cash replay, but compare it both with the harness baselines (the bar) and with the engine's own re-sim of the baselines on real. Report option net, worst day, max DD and futures net for every set and half, plus Switch-1.

tests.name: Nifty intraday realised-volatility state: hold for the big move on active days, bank T1 or skip on quiet days (Gao-Han-Li-Zhou; Li-Sakkas-Urquhart)
tests.hypothesis: Intraday momentum pays mainly on high-volatility days and is nearly absent on quiet ones. Gao et al., out of sample, report timing Sharpe of 0.18, 0.97 and 1.63 across first-half-hour realised-volatility terciles, and Li-Sakkas-Urquhart find the same in 16 markets. A bought option needs a big move to beat costs and decay. Holding Fable-OP's T3 only when the market is moving abnormally, and banking T1 (or skipping) on quiet days, should raise option net and cut losing chop days. This is a volatility state, unlike the trend regimes already tried.
tests.exact_rules: Nifty index 1-minute candles from H.minute_data(), loaded once. Sessions with fewer than 300 Nifty bars (e.g. Muhurat) are excluded from all histories. For day d and signal bar t (column 'time'): RV(d,t) = sqrt(sum of r_i^2), where r_0 = ln(C_09:15/O_09:15) and r_i = ln(C_i/C_{i-1}) for bars 09:16..t inclusive. rv_ratio = RV(d,t) / mean of RV(d',t) at the same clock bar over the 14 previous full sessions; at least 10 are needed, else NaN. pd_ratio (fully pre-open) = full-session RV of day d-1 (bars 09:15-15:29) / mean full-session RV over the 14 sessions before d-1. q33 = the 33rd percentile of rv_ratio over ALL A/B rows of the real design window (12 May-31 Aug), frozen. Specs: S1 def f(df): t = H.pick(df,'s_fable_op',75,6); t['pol'] = np.where(t.rv_ratio >= 1.0, 'T3', 'T1'); return t. S2: score = s_fable_op masked to NaN where rv_ratio < q33, then pick(...,75,6) and pol T3; masking happens before pick, so later signals can take the slots. S3: t = H.pick(df,'s_opus_v3',75,6); pol = CLOSE_TR where rv_ratio >= 1.0, else T1. S4: as S1 with pd_ratio in place of rv_ratio. NaN ratio: keep the base policy (T3 for S1/S2/S4, T1 for S3). Uses the harness opt_<pol> and net_<pol> columns, so real is judged on the real futures path. Only Nifty bars up to and including the signal bar and earlier sessions are used. H.regime() 'chg' is never used.
tests.fixed_params: Realised vol from 1-minute log returns (Gao). Tercile cut-off (33rd percentile) as in Gao's sort. 14-session, time-of-day-matched normalisation (the Zarattini noise-area lookback). Ratio cut 1.0 = an average day. Exits are the harness policies: Fable-OP base T3, Opus v3 base T1.
tests.grid: S1: Fable-OP>=75, T3 if rv_ratio>=1 else T1. S2: Fable-OP>=75, skip rows with rv_ratio < q33, T3. S3: Opus v3>=75, CLOSE_TR if rv_ratio>=1 else T1. S4: S1 using the prior-session ratio pd_ratio. Choose on real 12 May-31 Aug by option net, subject to design worst day and max DD no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline (else highest net, flagged).
tests.exit_policy: Per-row switch between existing harness policies: T3 (or CLOSE_TR for S3) on active days, T1 on quiet days. S2 keeps T3 and skips quiet-day signals.
tests.selection: Live rule: per day in time order, the first 6 rows whose (possibly masked) score >= 75. The switch changes only the exit, except in S2.
tests.compare_on: All three sets from the harness columns: unseen and real 2nd half for the bar, real 1st half and known for reference (known shares the design dates). The Nifty minutes cover 15 Oct 2025-12 Nov 2026, so every set is covered. Report option net, worst day, max DD, futures net and Switch-1.

tests.name: Stock-level noise-area filter: take a signal only when its move is abnormal for that stock at that minute (Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon), as the 'fast, large move' selection for bought options
tests.hypothesis: Options pay when the move after entry is big and quick. The noise-area paper defines a real imbalance as a move outside the stock's average absolute move from the open at that clock minute over the last 14 days, measured from the gap-adjusted reference max/min(open, previous close). Fable-OP scales the move by daily ATR and from the previous close, which ignores both the time of day and the gap side. That matters because 75 % of Fable-OP picks are at 09:17-09:20, when ATR scaling says least. Requiring an abnormal move should drop opening fake-outs, whose options bleed, and keep the trend-day starts.
tests.exact_rules: Cash data from H.minute_data(), loaded once, for ALL sets. As a feature this is valid for real too. Sessions with fewer than 300 bars are excluded from histories. For stock s, day d, signal bar k (column 'time'): O_d = open of the 09:15 bar of d. Cprev = close of the last daily candle dated before d. P = close of bar k on d. sigma_k = mean over the stock's 14 previous full sessions of |close at bar k (forward-filled from the last earlier bar if k is missing) / that day's 09:15 open - 1|. At least 10 sessions are needed, else NaN. LONG: noise_x = (P / max(O_d, Cprev) - 1) / sigma_k. SHORT: noise_x = (1 - P / min(O_d, Cprev)) / sigma_k. Specs (mask before pick, so later signals may take slots): S1 score = s_fable_op where noise_x >= 1.0 else NaN, pick(...,75,6), pol T3. S2 as S1 with noise_x >= 1.5. S3 score = s_fable_op + 10*clip(noise_x - 1, -1, 1), pick(...,75,6), T3. S4 score = s_opus_v3 where noise_x >= 1.0, pick(...,75,6), T1. NaN noise_x: the row passes the filter (S1/S2/S4) and is unadjusted (S3); report the count. Uses the harness opt_<pol>/net_<pol> columns.
tests.fixed_params: Lookback 14 sessions; move = |Close_HH:MM / Open_day - 1| averaged by clock minute; reference max(Open, prev Close) for longs and min for shorts (gap adjustment); volatility multiplier VM = 1 (paper) and 1.5 (the paper's best risk-adjusted). The paper's HH:00/HH:30 decision grid is not applied, because the scanner's own signal minutes are kept.
tests.grid: S1: Fable-OP>=75 AND noise_x>=1.0, T3. S2: Fable-OP>=75 AND noise_x>=1.5, T3. S3: s_fable_op + 10*clip(noise_x-1,-1,1) >= 75, T3. S4: Opus v3>=75 AND noise_x>=1.0, T1. Choose on real 12 May-31 Aug by option net, subject to design worst day and max DD no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline (else highest net, flagged).
tests.exit_policy: Unchanged harness policies: T3 for the Fable-OP based settings, T1 for the Opus v3 setting.
tests.selection: Live rule: per day in time order (ties: higher score, then symbol), the first 6 rows whose filtered or adjusted score >= 75.
tests.compare_on: All three sets from the harness columns (filter on existing rows). Real is judged on the real futures path. The bar is on unseen and real 2nd half. The first unseen sessions (from 3 Nov 2025) have about 11-13 prior sessions of minutes, which is enough for the 10-session minimum. Report option net, worst day, max DD, futures net and Switch-1.

tests.name: Meta-labelling for option profit: shallow gradient-boosted trees stacked on both scores, labelled on the option result, quantile gate at the baseline's selection rate (Lopez de Prado; Singh & Joubert; Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk)
tests.hypothesis: Meta-labelling helps only when the secondary model sees information the primary lacks. s_opus and s_fable_op are nearly uncorrelated (rho about 0.04 on the design window), and the signal list itself carries crowd information (same-side and opposite-side signals so far today) plus option-specific context (days to expiry) that neither score uses. A constrained non-linear secondary model, trained to predict a positive OPTION result under the exit actually used, should rank the high-recall A/B list better than either hand-built score at the same selection rate. This differs from the failed L2 logistic for T1: it uses trees, stacks both scores, adds crowd and expiry features, and uses an option label.
tests.exact_rules: Universe: all A/B rows. Features (no outcome columns, no REAL_ONLY columns): the 20 COMMON columns except 'price' (day_chg, gap, from_open, pos, beyond_pd, beyond_vwap, rel_vol, n_break, rsi14, vs20, ret5, ret20, nifty_chg, mins_since_extreme, minutes_since_open, atr_pct, from_52w_high, from_52w_low, risk_pct, stop_atr); side (LONG=1); s_opus; s_fable_op; a one-hot of H.regime()['A'] for the day; H.regime()['r20']; n_same_so_far = A/B rows of the same side that day with time < this row's time; n_opp_so_far = the same for the opposite side; n_same_minute = other rows with the same day and time; dte = calendar days from day to o_expiry. Labels: y = 1[opt_T3 > 0] (settings a, c, d) or 1[opt_T1 > 0] (setting b); outcomes are used as labels only. Model (a, b, d): lightgbm.LGBMClassifier(num_leaves=7, max_depth=3, min_child_samples=80, learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=300, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.7, reg_lambda=10, path_smooth=20, monotone_constraints=+1 on s_opus and s_fable_op and 0 elsewhere, random_state=0). Model (c): per side, LogisticRegression(C=1.0) on standardised [s_opus, s_fable_op, s_opus*s_fable_op]. Training: real design window rows only (12 May-31 Aug; 2,746 rows, 78 days). Out-of-fold p on the design rows from GroupKFold(5) grouped by day, then Platt (sigmoid) calibration fitted on those OOF predictions (per side for c). The final model is refit on all design rows and applied to every other row of every set. Gate: thr = the quantile of design OOF p such that the share of design rows with p >= thr equals the baseline's design selection rate: 5.97 % (the s_fable_op>=75 rate) for a and c, 8.23 % (the s_opus_v3>=75 rate) for b, and 9.0 % for d. Trades: H.pick(df, 'p_meta', thr, 6). Design-window rows are scored with their OOF p (never in-sample p) for the design evaluation and setting choice.
tests.fixed_params: Meta-labelling structure (high-recall primary = every A/B signal, secondary predicts whether the trade pays, trade only above a top-quantile probability) from AFML via Singh & Joubert and Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk (top-quantile gate). Platt rather than isotonic calibration because there are far fewer than 1,000 calibration samples (sklearn guidance). Tree hyperparameters as listed, not tuned. Gate rates are taken from the baselines' own design selection rates.
tests.grid: (a) GBDT, y = opt_T3>0, gate 5.97 %, exit T3. (b) GBDT, y = opt_T1>0, gate 8.23 %, exit T1. (c) Per-side logistic stacker on the two scores and their product, y = opt_T3>0, gate 5.97 %, exit T3. (d) As (a) with gate 9.0 % (1.5x the rate, more trades). Choose on the design window using OOF predictions, by option net, subject to design worst day and max DD no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline (else highest net, flagged).
tests.exit_policy: T3 for settings a, c and d; T1 for setting b (harness columns).
tests.selection: Score = calibrated meta probability p_meta; threshold = the frozen design quantile above; per day in time order, the first 6 rows with p_meta >= thr.
tests.compare_on: Train on real 12 May-31 Aug only. The test sets are unseen (the cash stand-in, so calibration shift is possible; the quantile gate is fixed in p, not re-fitted) and real 2nd half. Known shares the design dates, so it is reported only as a contaminated cross-check. Report option net, worst day, max DD, futures net, Switch-1, the realised selection rate per set, and the OOF design AUC.

tests.name: Equal option-risk lot sizing at the baseline's total premium outlay (delta-times-stop loss per contract with a 20 % pad; reduce size rather than tighten the stop)
tests.hypothesis: Futures sizing equalises the FUTURES loss at the stop. The bought option's loss at that same stop is (delta*R - 0.5*gamma*R^2 + decay + costs), which varies widely: small where the stop is wide relative to the option's implied move (strong convexity cushion), large where it is tight (all decay and spread). Sizing each trade so that the modelled option loss at the stop is equal moves lots toward trades whose option asymmetry is best. Holding total premium outlay at the baseline's level makes this a reallocation rather than added leverage. The brief names lot count for a bought option as an open lever.
tests.exact_rules: Picks unchanged: t = H.pick(df, S, 75, 6), S = 's_fable_op' (exit T3) or 's_opus_v3' (exit T1). Per picked row: call = (o_kind=='CE'); sgn = +1 if call else -1; F0 = o_F0; K = F0 (ATM, as the scanner); T0 = H._years(o_entry_ts, o_expiry); s = o_iv; p0 = H._b76(F0, K, T0, s, call); pS = H._b76(F0 - sgn*o_risk_abs, K, T0, s, call), the premium with the underlying at the futures stop and no decay (the pad covers decay, IV and spread). lot: column 'lot' on unseen/known. On real, the known set's 'lot' for the same symbol on the nearest date <= day (else the nearest after); if o_qty % lot != 0, lot = o_qty (treated as one lot). fut_lots = o_qty/lot. Per-lot option loss at the stop: Ll = 1.2*(p0 - pS)*lot + H.opt_costs(p0, pS, lot). New lots L = clip(floor(B/Ll), 1, cap*fut_lots). pnl = H.option_net(t, pol, qty=L*lot); outlay = H.option_net(t, pol, qty=L*lot, detail=True).outlay. The trade function returns t with this 'pnl' column (harness run() keeps a supplied pnl); futures reference = net_<pol> * L/fut_lots. Capital-neutral budget B_eq: bisection over Rs 1,000-60,000 (tolerance Rs 10) on the DESIGN-window picks of that setting only, so that sum(new outlay) = sum(p0*o_qty) for the same picks. B_eq is then frozen and applied unchanged to all sets.
tests.fixed_params: Loss per contract = move to the stop through the option's price sensitivity (Black-76 repricing in place of delta*distance), padded 20 % (Tradefundrr). Lots = planned risk / backstop loss per contract (Tradefundrr; EPAT floor-to-whole-lots). The underlying (futures) stop and exit are kept; only size changes (Quantsapp: reduce size rather than tighten the stop). Rs 15,000 risk budget, ATM monthly contract and roll rule as the scanner.
tests.grid: (a) Fable-OP>=75, T3, cap 2x futures lots, B = B_eq. (b) Fable-OP>=75, T3, cap 3x, B = B_eq. (c) Opus v3>=75, T1, cap 3x, B = B_eq (its own B_eq). (d) Fable-OP>=75, T3, cap 3x, B = Rs 15,000 of modelled option loss at the stop: the brief's literal 'same Rs 15,000 risk', with more capital. Choose on the design window by option net, but only among settings whose design option worst day and max DD are no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline (else highest net, flagged). Setting (d) is always reported separately as a leverage variant.
tests.exit_policy: Unchanged: T3 for the Fable-OP settings, T1 for the Opus v3 setting; the option is sold the minute after the futures leg exits.
tests.selection: The baseline live rule unchanged (first 6 per day with score >= 75 in time order); only the option quantity per trade changes.
tests.compare_on: All three sets. Unseen and known have exact lot sizes. Real uses lots inferred from the known set (exact for dates up to 19 Oct, latest known lot after that). The bar is on unseen and real 2nd half. Because lot count changes, report separately: premium outlay per trade (mean, median, max), the largest single-day total outlay, total outlay vs the baseline, option worst day and max DD, plus futures net at the new lots for reference.

tests.name: Prior-day range compression bonus (NR4 / NR7 / triangle) and no same-direction trade after a prior trend day (Zarattini et al. Table 5; Crabel; Unofficed NR7 F&O test)
tests.hypothesis: A breakout out of a compressed prior-day range is a volatility-expansion event with room left to its typical daily range. That suits a bought option, which needs the move to happen. After a full trend day in the same direction, next-day momentum fails. Zarattini et al. report next-day intraday-momentum P&L of 22 bps (t 5.1) after NR4, 16 bps after NR7 and 14 bps after triangles, against 12 bps unconditional, and -2 bps (Sharpe -0.3) after trend days. No current score or harness feature uses prior-day range patterns.
tests.exact_rules: Cash daily candles from H.minute_data() (from Jan 2024), using only candles dated before d. Short sessions (fewer than 300 Nifty minute bars, e.g. Muhurat) are dropped before computing patterns. Index the last k full sessions before d as d-1, d-2, ...; rng = High - Low. NR4: rng[d-1] == min(rng[d-4..d-1]). NR7: rng[d-1] == min(rng[d-7..d-1]). Triangle: High[d-1] < min(High[d-2], High[d-3]) and Low[d-1] > max(Low[d-2], Low[d-3]). compressed = NR4 or NR7 or Triangle. Trend day in trade direction: for a LONG, Open[d-1] <= Low[d-1] + 0.15*rng[d-1] and Close[d-1] >= Low[d-1] + 0.85*rng[d-1] and rng[d-1] > mean(rng over the 14 sessions before d-1); for a SHORT, Open[d-1] >= Low[d-1] + 0.85*rng[d-1] and Close[d-1] <= Low[d-1] + 0.15*rng[d-1] and the same range condition. Fewer than 16 prior sessions: no flags. Specs (adjust or mask before pick): S1 score = s_fable_op + 10*compressed, pick(...,75,6), T3. S2 score = s_fable_op, NaN where trend_day_same_dir, pick(...,75,6), T3. S3 = S1 and S2 together, T3. S4 = S3 applied to s_opus_v3, T1. Uses the harness opt_<pol>/net_<pol> columns.
tests.fixed_params: NR4 (4 days), NR7 (7 days), triangle with a 2-day lookback, trend day at the 15/85 % range positions with range above the 14-day mean (all from the paper's Table 5 definitions). The bonus of +10 points is the size the candidate declared, set so that 65-74 signals can enter on compressed days; it is not tuned.
tests.grid: S1: +10 bonus when compressed (Fable-OP, T3). S2: drop signals after a same-direction trend day (Fable-OP, T3). S3: S1 + S2 (Fable-OP, T3). S4: S1 + S2 on Opus v3 (T1). Choose on real 12 May-31 Aug by option net, subject to design worst day and max DD no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline (else highest net, flagged).
tests.exit_policy: Unchanged harness policies: T3 for the Fable-OP settings, T1 for the Opus v3 setting.
tests.selection: Live rule: per day in time order (ties: higher adjusted score, then symbol), the first 6 rows whose adjusted or masked score >= 75.
tests.compare_on: All three sets from the harness columns (pre-open flags on existing rows); real is judged on the real futures path. The bar is on unseen and real 2nd half; known is reported as a cross-check. Report flag frequencies per set, option net, worst day, max DD, futures net and Switch-1.

rejected.reason: High overlap with v3's rel_vol gate. Fable-OP picks at 09:17-09:20 already have a median rel_vol of 2.6, so the gate barely binds, and the short extension touches about 11 % of Fable-OP picks.

rejected.reason: The published effect is about 5 bps, under 0.1R, on the few trades still open at 15:00. Fable-OP picks are 89 % long, and there is no Indian evidence.

rejected.reason: Folklore-grade: no published statistics anywhere. The prior-day range idea is tested with published table evidence in prior_compression.

rejected.reason: Merged into prior_compression (same NR4/NR7 compression flags, with Zarattini's table definitions).

rejected.reason: The only Indian figure is about breakeven (50 % at 1.3 RR, no costs), and the condition is nearly automatic for the 09:17-09:20 signals that make up about 75 % of Fable-OP picks.

rejected.reason: No intraday evidence; the only costed Indian test (monthly rotation) failed; it needs 28 manual sector tags and conflicts with Fable-OP's idiosyncratic-move component.

rejected.reason: About 6 expiries per set gives almost no statistical power. The evidence is from 20 years ago, before physical settlement, and a second study found no effect. The scanner already rolls to next month at 4 sessions or fewer.

rejected.reason: Published evidence shows sizing shrinks losses without creating edge. Under a net-profit bar, halving positive-EV trades lowers net, and with 63 % one-lot picks half size means skip.

rejected.reason: 78 design queries is far too few. The live rule takes the first 6 in time order, so within-day ranking cannot be used without look-ahead.

rejected.reason: Anonymous blog source on index CFDs with undisclosed setups and costs. Breakeven-step variants have already failed on this system, and the better-evidenced trailing idea is tested in vwap_trail.

rejected.name: #27 Nifty RSI(5) as a dealer-gamma proxy
rejected.reason: No Indian market is in the gamma evidence, India's option-market structure differs (retail buyers, prop sellers), and it is correlated with r20 and the trend gates that already failed.

rejected.name: #28 Daily loss limit after 2 stop-outs or -2R
rejected.reason: Anecdotal evidence: one MNQ backtest with no with/without comparison. The bought option already caps per-trade losses.

rejected.name: #29 Constant-delta strike (|delta| about 0.65)
rejected.reason: Overlaps the lead's fixed-strike grid. Most of the ITM 'edge' is extra delta per lot (leverage), and the model has no skew, so ITM-call gains are overstated.

rejected.name: #30 Days-to-expiry next-month switch
rejected.reason: The lead's grid already covers std vs next. For intraday holds the gamma-theta break-even is independent of days to expiry, so any modelled gain would come from constant-IV, no-term-structure, no-liquidity assumptions rather than an edge.

rejected.name: #31 Intraday realised-vs-implied pace filter (RV/IV)
rejected.reason: Not used: RV is undefined or noisy for the 09:17-09:20 signals (2-3 minute returns) that make up about 75 % of Fable-OP picks, and model IV is a fixed function of ATR, so the 'IV cheap' channel is invisible. The fast, abnormal move selection is tested through noise_area.

rejected.reason: (a) changes the cost model rather than the strategy, so it is not like-for-like with the baselines, and skipping pre-09:45 removes about 90 % of Fable-OP picks; (b) the post-noon call/put asymmetry is an IV effect that the constant-IV model cannot see.

rejected.name: #34 Spot-vol (vega) side filter
rejected.reason: Untestable: the mechanism is vega P&L, and the harness prices entry and exit with one IV and has no real IV history.

rejected.name: #35 Skip option buys when IV is rich (results days, IV/RV rank)
rejected.reason: Untestable with cached data: no results calendar and no option bhavcopy or daily IV per stock.

rejected.name: #36 Option-liquidity screen with tiered slippage
rejected.reason: Its gain comes from charging the candidate different costs than the baselines. Under the uniform 0.25 % model it can only remove trades; it belongs as a robustness check on every candidate, not as a test.

Peeks (no profit figures were computed):
- Design window: 2,746 A/B rows over 78 days.
- Selection rates: s_fable_op>=75 is 5.97 %, s_opus_v3>=75 is 8.23 %.
- Fable-OP picks: median 3 minutes after the open (75 % within 5 minutes), 89 % long, 2.46 a day on average. The cap of 6 binds on only 2 of 78 days, so filters remove trades and bonuses add them.
- About 80 % of Fable-OP picks are also v3 picks.
- 63 % of Fable-OP picks are one lot on unseen and known.
- Days to expiry run 7-36 (median 21).

Option net under the harness model is the objective; futures net is reported as secondary.

Common protocol for all six tests:
1. Choose among each test's at most 4 settings on real 12 May-31 Aug only. The criterion is the highest option net among settings whose design-window option worst day and max DD are no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline; if none qualifies, take the highest net and flag it.
2. The bar is judged on unseen and real 2nd half against Opus v3 (T1) and Fable-OP (T3) option net, with risk no worse than 1.25x the better baseline.
3. Report Switch-1, every set and half, and futures net. Known shares the design dates, so it is a cross-check only, and it is contaminated for the ML test.
4. Load the minute data at most once per process.
5. Exclude short sessions (fewer than 300 bars, e.g. Muhurat) from all histories, including daily-pattern flags. 9 Nov 2026 in real 2nd half would otherwise be flagged NR4/NR7 off a Muhurat candle.
6. Never use outcome columns as features.
7. Work only in $SP/hunt/<id>/.

spec.name: VWAP trailing exit with no target, flat at 15:29 (noise-area paper's trail, cut down to the VWAP leg), on Fable-OP picks
spec.hypothesis: A bought option has a convex payoff, so it gains most from letting trend-day winners run and from cutting non-performers before the structural stop. Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon's VWAP trail with no target halved the worst day and doubled Sharpe against a loose fixed stop (SPY, in sample), and the ORB papers find exit-at-close beats every fixed R target. Replacing Fable-OP's fixed T3 with a VWAP trail should lift option net by keeping the right tail and trimming afternoon give-backs and slow losers.
spec.exact_rules: Picks: t = H.pick(df, S, 75, 6) with S = 's_fable_op' (S1-S3) or 's_opus_v3' (S4). Data: mins, daily, nifty, lot = H.minute_data(), loaded once per process; cash minutes of t.symbol on t.day. sgn = +1 LONG, -1 SHORT. Entry minute e = the bar after the signal bar (signal bar = column 'time'), E = open of bar e. Structural stop in cash: unseen/known use column 'stop'; real uses stop_c = E*(1 - sgn*o_risk_abs/o_F0). R = |E - stop_c|. Session VWAP_k = cumsum(((H+L+C)/3)*V)/cumsum(V) over bars 09:15..k (cash, regular session only). Walk bars k = e, e+1, ...: (1) Stop first: if a long bar's low <= stop_c (short: high >= stop_c), exit at stop_c, or at the bar's open if it opens beyond the stop. Gap handling is copied from scanner.equity.fills.simulate. (2) VWAP rule, only at the CHECK bars and only if not stopped in that bar: if a long's close < VWAP_k (short's close > VWAP_k), exit at the open of bar k+1. (3) Anything still open is squared off at 15:29 exactly as fills.simulate does for the CLOSE policy. No profit target. Option leg: set t['o_F1_VW'] = o_F0 * (X/E), where X is the cash exit price (this maps the cash move onto the scanner's underlying; exact on unseen/known, approximate on real), and t['o_exit_ts_VW'] = the exit bar timestamp in the same ISO +05:30 format as o_exit_ts_*. Then pnl = H.option_net(t, 'VW'), which applies the harness's 1-minute exit lag. Futures (reference): unseen/known lots*lot*sgn*(X-E) minus scanner.equity.costs.round_trip and costs.slippage(..., 0.02). Real: sgn*(X/E-1)*o_F0*o_qty minus the same costs. ENGINE CHECK, mandatory and reported before any VW result: with the VWAP rule disabled the engine must reproduce the harness CLOSE policy (o_F1_CLOSE, o_exit_ts_CLOSE, opt_CLOSE) on unseen/known within rounding. Also report the engine's own CLOSE and T3/T1 re-sim on real, so that engine differences are not counted as exit gains.
spec.fixed_params: VWAP from regular-session 1-minute data, recomputed every minute (paper). No profit target; flat at the close (both papers). Check grid every 30 minutes, as in the paper's HH:00/HH:30 checks (NSE opens 09:15, so checks are at the closes of the bars stamped 09:44, 10:14, ..., 15:14). The scanner's structural stop, entry at the next minute's open, Rs 15,000 futures-risk lots, max 6 a day and option costs/slippage as in the harness are kept unchanged. The paper's band leg (max(UpperBound, VWAP)) is dropped because scanner entries are not noise-band breaks, so most would exit at once.
spec.grid: S1: s_fable_op>=75 picks, VWAP checked at the 30-minute marks only (bars 09:44, 10:14, ..., 15:14), active from entry. S2: s_fable_op>=75, VWAP checked at every 1-minute close from the entry bar. S3: s_fable_op>=75, 1-minute checks, active only once MFE >= +0.5R (MFE from bar highs/lows since entry, in R). S4: s_opus_v3>=75 picks, as S1. Choose on the real design window (12 May-31 Aug, cash re-sim of the real picks): highest option net among the settings whose design option worst day and max DD are no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline; if none qualifies, take the highest net and flag it.
spec.exit_policy: New per-row policy 'VW': structural stop always live, plus a VWAP trail (exit at the next bar's open after a check-bar close beyond VWAP against the trade), no target, square-off at 15:29. The option is sold at the open of the minute after the futures exit (harness exit_lag_min = 1).
spec.selection: Live rule unchanged: per day in time order (ties by higher score, then symbol), the first 6 rows with s_fable_op >= 75 (S1-S3) or s_opus_v3 >= 75 (S4).
spec.compare_on: Clean like-for-like on unseen (bar set) and known (cash stand-in; the engine reproduces the harness CLOSE policy there). On real, and so on real 2nd half (bar set), it is a cash re-sim of the real picks mapped onto o_F0. That matches how the harness itself already times real-set exits from a cash replay, but compare it both with the harness baselines (the bar) and with the engine's own re-sim of the baselines on real. Report option net, worst day, max DD and futures net for every set and half, plus Switch-1.

result.deviations: No rule deviations. Implementation notes: (1) On real, stop_c = E*(1 - sgn*o_risk_abs/o_F0) is used unrounded, as specified. Floating-point noise on bars whose high or low equals the stop to the tick changes the exit minute against the harness's own cash replay on 6 of 4,996 real rows (1 of the 384 picked rows). I also tried rounding stop_c to 4 decimals: it gave 15 mismatches, so I reverted it. (2) The design-window stats come from H.run + H.stats on the real rows dated 12 May-31 Aug only. H.evaluate on that subset crashes on the empty 2nd half. The numbers are identical to evaluate()'s real 'h1' (for example Fable-OP T3 +347,343, Opus v3 T1 +239,288). (3) The 'VW' trades carry net_VW (futures), r_VW (cash R) and pnl (H.option_net with pol 'E<rule>', which uses o_F1_E* = o_F0*X/E and o_exit_ts_E* = the exit bar's ISO timestamp, plus the harness's 1-minute exit lag). After a VWAP trigger at the close of bar k, the futures leg exits at the open of k+1 and the option sells at the open of k+2. (4) For the engine's T1/T3 re-sim on real, targets come from price/risk_pct, the same way the harness's optlayer cash replay does it.
result.design_window_choice: S3 (s_fable_op>=75, VWAP checked at every 1-minute close, only once MFE >= +0.5R). Design window = real 12 May-31 Aug 2026, option net. Risk limits: worst day >= -23,578 (1.25 x the better baseline's -18,863, Opus v3) and max DD >= -35,690 (1.25 x -28,552, Fable-OP). S1: +362,530, wd -14,886, DD -47,176, fails on DD. S2: +187,768, -10,427, -25,242, qualifies. S3: +371,599, -12,539, -27,076, qualifies, highest net, chosen. S4: +296,766, -14,886, -47,429, fails on DD. Baselines on the design window: Opus v3 T1 +239,288 and Fable-OP T3 +347,343; the engine's own re-sims are +279,205 and +351,461. No flag was needed.
result.summary:
The VWAP trail fails the bar: it beats both baselines on unseen but loses to both on real 2nd half.

Engine check: with the VWAP rule off, the engine reproduces the harness CLOSE, T1 and T3 exactly on unseen and known (exit times match 100%, F1 and option/futures per-row differences 0.00, all rows). It also agrees with scanner fills.simulate on every picked row of all 3 sets (0 mismatches), and an independent bar-by-bar loop (verify.py) agrees on all 3 VW rules (0 mismatches). On real, the engine's own re-sim is close to the harness: Fable-OP T3 +5,43,244 vs +5,45,031; real h2 +1,91,783 vs +1,97,688.

Chosen on the design window: S3 (Fable-OP picks, 1-minute VWAP checks, active once MFE >= 0.5R).

Results, modelled OPTION net:
- **Unseen:** +3,09,165 (worst day -16,461, max DD -22,488, futures +2,79,380). It beats Opus v3 T1 (+84,362), Fable-OP T3 (+2,02,948) and Switch-1 (+2,67,606).
- **Real 2nd half:** +1,33,080 (worst day -14,865, max DD -29,254, futures +1,55,968). It loses to Opus v3 T1 (+1,84,693), Fable-OP T3 (+1,97,688) and Switch-1 (+2,43,042). It also loses like-for-like to the engine's own re-sims (Fable-OP T3 +1,91,783, Opus v3 T1 +1,53,593).
- **Real full:** +5,04,679 vs +4,23,981 / +5,45,031 / +5,82,910.
- **Known:** +85,438 vs +1,99,051 / +1,83,848; known 2nd half -49,959.

Risk is within the 1.25x limits on unseen and real h2.

How it trades: the trail cuts the median hold to about 60-66 minutes, against about 264-310 minutes for T3. Of the 233 real trades, 136 exit on the VWAP rule, 52 at the stop and 45 at the close. It helped in Nov-Feb and May-Aug and hurt in Sep-Nov 2026 (real h2 and known h2).
result.caveats:
1. **Real-set timing:** on real (and so real h2), exits come from a cash re-sim mapped onto o_F0. The harness baselines use the real futures R, so compare against the engine re-sims as well; the candidate loses on real h2 on both comparisons. 6 of 4,996 real rows (1 of 384 picks) exit a minute away from the harness cash replay because of float noise on bars that exactly touch the stop.

2. **Option model:** option figures are modelled, roughly +-10%, with no skew. The VW exits are much earlier, so less time decay is charged; the result depends on the decay fit.

3. **Unseen gain sits in the 1st half:** the unseen gain is concentrated in unseen h1 (+2,02,376 vs Fable-OP +83,843). In unseen h2 the candidate is +1,06,789, below Fable-OP T3 (+1,19,104) and Switch-1 (+1,81,893).

4. **Declared settings not chosen (shown in run.log for information only):**
   - S1 (Fable-OP, 30-minute checks): unseen +2,99,929, real h2 +1,81,534. It fails real h2.
   - S2 (Fable-OP, 1-minute checks): unseen +2,52,292, real h2 +81,251.
   - S4 (Opus v3, 30-minute checks): unseen +2,80,717, real h2 +2,48,973. On net it would clear both baselines and Switch-1 on both test sets. spec.name: Nifty intraday realised-volatility state: hold for the big move on active days, bank T1 or skip on quiet days (Gao-Han-Li-Zhou; Li-Sakkas-Urquhart)
spec.hypothesis: Intraday momentum pays mainly on high-volatility days and is nearly absent on quiet ones. Gao et al., out of sample, report timing Sharpe of 0.18, 0.97 and 1.63 across first-half-hour realised-volatility terciles, and Li-Sakkas-Urquhart find the same in 16 markets. A bought option needs a big move to beat costs and decay. Holding Fable-OP's T3 only when the market is moving abnormally, and banking T1 (or skipping) on quiet days, should raise option net and cut losing chop days. This is a volatility state, unlike the trend regimes already tried.
spec.exact_rules: Nifty index 1-minute candles from H.minute_data(), loaded once. Sessions with fewer than 300 Nifty bars (e.g. Muhurat) are excluded from all histories. For day d and signal bar t (column 'time'): RV(d,t) = sqrt(sum of r_i^2), where r_0 = ln(C_09:15/O_09:15) and r_i = ln(C_i/C_{i-1}) for bars 09:16..t inclusive. rv_ratio = RV(d,t) / mean of RV(d',t) at the same clock bar over the 14 previous full sessions; at least 10 are needed, else NaN. pd_ratio (fully pre-open) = full-session RV of day d-1 (bars 09:15-15:29) / mean full-session RV over the 14 sessions before d-1. q33 = the 33rd percentile of rv_ratio over ALL A/B rows of the real design window (12 May-31 Aug), frozen. Specs: S1 def f(df): t = H.pick(df,'s_fable_op',75,6); t['pol'] = np.where(t.rv_ratio >= 1.0, 'T3', 'T1'); return t. S2: score = s_fable_op masked to NaN where rv_ratio < q33, then pick(...,75,6) and pol T3; masking happens before pick, so later signals can take the slots. S3: t = H.pick(df,'s_opus_v3',75,6); pol = CLOSE_TR where rv_ratio >= 1.0, else T1. S4: as S1 with pd_ratio in place of rv_ratio. NaN ratio: keep the base policy (T3 for S1/S2/S4, T1 for S3). Uses the harness opt_<pol> and net_<pol> columns, so real is judged on the real futures path. Only Nifty bars up to and including the signal bar and earlier sessions are used. H.regime() 'chg' is never used.
spec.fixed_params: Realised vol from 1-minute log returns (Gao). Tercile cut-off (33rd percentile) as in Gao's sort. 14-session, time-of-day-matched normalisation (the Zarattini noise-area lookback). Ratio cut 1.0 = an average day. Exits are the harness policies: Fable-OP base T3, Opus v3 base T1.
spec.grid: S1: Fable-OP>=75, T3 if rv_ratio>=1 else T1. S2: Fable-OP>=75, skip rows with rv_ratio < q33, T3. S3: Opus v3>=75, CLOSE_TR if rv_ratio>=1 else T1.
