spec.name: Stock-level noise-area filter: take a signal only when its move is abnormal for that stock at that minute (Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon), as the 'fast, large move' selection for bought options
spec.hypothesis: Options pay when the move after entry is big and quick. The noise-area paper defines a real imbalance as a move outside the stock's average absolute move from the open at that clock minute over the last 14 days, measured from the gap-adjusted reference max/min(open, previous close). Fable-OP scales the move by daily ATR and from the previous close, which ignores both the time of day and the gap side. That matters because 75 % of Fable-OP picks are at 09:17-09:20, when ATR scaling says least. Requiring an abnormal move should drop opening fake-outs, whose options bleed, and keep the trend-day starts.
spec.exact_rules: Cash data from H.minute_data(), loaded once, for ALL sets. As a feature this is valid for real too. Sessions with fewer than 300 bars are excluded from histories. For stock s, day d, signal bar k (column 'time'): O_d = open of the 09:15 bar of d. Cprev = close of the last daily candle dated before d. P = close of bar k on d. sigma_k = mean over the stock's 14 previous full sessions of |close at bar k (forward-filled from the last earlier bar if k is missing) / that day's 09:15 open - 1|. At least 10 sessions are needed, else NaN. LONG: noise_x = (P / max(O_d, Cprev) - 1) / sigma_k. SHORT: noise_x = (1 - P / min(O_d, Cprev)) / sigma_k. Specs (mask before pick, so later signals may take slots): S1 score = s_fable_op where noise_x >= 1.0 else NaN, pick(...,75,6), pol T3. S2 as S1 with noise_x >= 1.5. S3 score = s_fable_op + 10*clip(noise_x - 1, -1, 1), pick(...,75,6), T3. S4 score = s_opus_v3 where noise_x >= 1.0, pick(...,75,6), T1. NaN noise_x: the row passes the filter (S1/S2/S4) and is unadjusted (S3); report the count. Uses the harness opt_<pol>/net_<pol> columns.
spec.fixed_params: Lookback 14 sessions; move = |Close_HH:MM / Open_day - 1| averaged by clock minute; reference max(Open, prev Close) for longs and min for shorts (gap adjustment); volatility multiplier VM = 1 (paper) and 1.5 (the paper's best risk-adjusted). spec.name: Meta-labelling for option profit: shallow gradient-boosted trees stacked on both scores, labelled on the option result, quantile gate at the baseline's selection rate (Lopez de Prado; Singh & Joubert; Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk)
spec.hypothesis: Meta-labelling helps only when the secondary model sees information the primary lacks. s_opus and s_fable_op are nearly uncorrelated (rho about 0.04 on the design window), and the signal list itself carries crowd information (same-side and opposite-side signals so far today) plus option-specific context (days to expiry) that neither score uses. A constrained non-linear secondary model, trained to predict a positive OPTION result under the exit actually used, should rank the high-recall A/B list better than either hand-built score at the same selection rate. This differs from the failed L2 logistic for T1: it uses trees, stacks both scores, adds crowd and expiry features, and uses an option label.
spec.exact_rules: Universe: all A/B rows. Features (no outcome columns, no REAL_ONLY columns): the 20 COMMON columns except 'price' (day_chg, gap, from_open, pos, beyond_pd, beyond_vwap, rel_vol, n_break, rsi14, vs20, ret5, ret20, nifty_chg, mins_since_extreme, minutes_since_open, atr_pct, from_52w_high, from_52w_low, risk_pct, stop_atr); side (LONG=1); s_opus; s_fable_op; a one-hot of H.regime()['A'] for the day; H.regime()['r20']; n_same_so_far = A/B rows of the same side that day with time < this row's time; n_opp_so_far = the same for the opposite side; n_same_minute = other rows with the same day and time; dte = calendar days from day to o_expiry. Labels: y = 1[opt_T3 > 0] (settings a, c, d) or 1[opt_T1 > 0] (setting b); outcomes are used as labels only. Model (a, b, d): lightgbm.LGBMClassifier(num_leaves=7, max_depth=3, min_child_samples=80, learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=300, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.7, reg_lambda=10, path_smooth=20, monotone_constraints=+1 on s_opus and s_fable_op and 0 elsewhere, random_state=0). Model (c): per side, LogisticRegression(C=1.0) on standardised [s_opus, s_fable_op, s_opus*s_fable_op]. Training: real design window rows only (12 May-31 Aug; 2,746 rows, 78 days). Out-of-fold p on the design rows from GroupKFold(5) grouped by day, then Platt (sigmoid) calibration fitted on those OOF predictions (per side for c). The final model is refit on all design rows and applied to every other row of every set. Gate: thr = the quantile of design OOF p such that the share of design rows with p >= thr equals the baseline's design selection rate: 5.97 % (the s_fable_op>=75 rate) for a and c, 8.23 % (the s_opus_v3>=75 rate) for b, and 9.0 % for d. Trades: H.pick(df, 'p_meta', thr, 6). Design-window rows are scored with their OOF p (never in-sample p) for the design evaluation and setting choice.
spec.fixed_params: Meta-labelling structure (high-recall primary = every A/B signal, secondary predicts whether the trade pays, trade only above a top-quantile probability) from AFML via Singh & Joubert and Korniejczuk & Slepaczuk (top-quantile gate). Platt rather than isotonic calibration because there are far fewer than 1,000 calibration samples (sklearn guidance). Tree hyperparameters as listed, not tuned. Gate rates are taken from the baselines' own design selection rates.
spec.grid: (a) GBDT, y = opt_T3>0, gate 5.97 %, exit T3. (b) GBDT, y = opt_T1>0, gate 8.23 %, exit T1. (c) Per-side logistic stacker on the two scores and their product, y = opt_T3>0, gate 5.97 %, exit T3. (d) As (a) with gate 9.0 % (1.5x the rate, more trades). Choose on the design window using OOF predictions, by option net, subject to design worst day and max DD no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline (else highest net, flagged).
spec.exit_policy: T3 for settings a, c and d; T1 for setting b (harness columns).
spec.selection: Score = calibrated meta probability p_meta; threshold = the frozen design quantile above; per day in time order, the first 6 rows with p_meta >= thr.
spec.compare_on: Train on real 12 May-31 Aug only. The test sets are unseen (the cash stand-in, so calibration shift is possible; the quantile gate is fixed in p, not re-fitted) and real 2nd half. Known shares the design dates, so it is reported only as a contaminated cross-check. Report option net, worst day, max DD, futures net, Switch-1, the realised selection rate per set, and the OOF design AUC.

result.deviations:
No change to the model. Only small, non-substantive additions and some interpretations:
(1) I added n_jobs=2, verbose=-1, deterministic=True and force_row_wise=True to LGBMClassifier, for reproducibility and to share the CPUs. All pre-registered hyperparameters are exactly as listed.
(2) Platt step = sklearn's _SigmoidCalibration, the same estimator CalibratedClassifierCV(method='sigmoid') uses. For the GBDT it is fitted on OOF predict_proba (LGBM has no decision_function, so this matches what CalibratedClassifierCV would use). For the per-side LR it is fitted on OOF decision_function, separately per side.
(3) Gate: k = round(rate x N_design) (164 / 226 / 164 / 247 rows) and thr = the k-th largest OOF p.
(4) 'Better design baseline' for the risk limit is taken per metric (the less negative worst day and the less negative max DD of Opus v3 T1 and Fable-OP T3 on the design window).
(5) In the final 'real' table, the first half (= the design window) uses OOF p and the second half uses the final refit model. In-sample p is never used.
(6) GroupKFold(5) is unshuffled (the default). Crowd counts (n_same_so_far, n_opp_so_far, n_same_minute) are counted within each set's own A/B signal list. The regime one-hot has 3 levels (Uptrend/Downtrend/Sideways).
(7) I added diagnostics: Platt slopes, raw OOF AUC, held-out AUC, selection-rate drift and calibration means. I also added one clearly labelled EXPLORATORY section, not pre-registered and not used for the choice.

1. The Platt step reverses the ranking. I implemented it literally (sklearn's sigmoid calibration, slope not constrained). Fitted slopes (p = expit(-(a*f+b)); a > 0 means the ranking is reversed):
- gbdt_T3: a = +1.069
- gbdt_T1: a = +0.0006
- LR short side: a = +0.275
- LR long side: a = -0.432 (ranking kept)
So settings a, b and d trade the rows the refit GBDT rates LEAST likely to pay. That is what the pre-registered procedure does when the OOF signal is below chance.

2. EXPLORATORY, not pre-registered, not used for any choice: the GBDT ranked by its raw probability, with no reversal and the same gate rates on the raw OOF quantile. It also fails. Option net, a / b / d:
- **Design:** +28,609 / -29,555 / -60,408 (design max DD -46,570 / -88,374 / -98,254, also failing the risk limit)
- **Unseen:** -11,064 / +23,453 / +64,830

That is pure contamination: the refit model's in-sample design AUC is 0.79, its AUC on known first half is 0.72, and known rows match real rows at 0.92 correlation of opt_T3. The same contamination, with the ranking reversed, explains the large known losses of a, b and d in the main table.

3. The selection rate drifted on held-out sets. Share of rows passing the gate, design / real 2nd half / unseen / known:
- a: 5.97 / 14.18 / 7.66 / 9.82 %
- b: 8.23 / 19.02 / 8.37 / 10.53 %
- c: 5.97 / 2.31 / 3.39 / 5.12 %
- d: 8.99 / 17.87 / 9.98 / 13.42 %

- real 2nd half: 4.44 / 5.33 / 2.31 / 5.56 %
- unseen: 3.15 / 2.75 / 3.39 / 4.02 %

5. The model learned mostly day-level structure. The top gain features are r20, dte, nifty_chg and from_52w_high. This fits a model that memorises days in sample and does not generalise.

6. Option figures are the harness's Black-76 model (good to roughly +-10 %). Unseen and known are cash stand-ins.

leakage_or_bugs: No look-ahead found. FEATS has the 20 COMMON columns without 'price', plus side, s_opus, s_fable_op, the regime one-hot, r20, the crowd counts and dte. None of these are outcome columns or REAL_ONLY columns. The crowd counts use strictly earlier times (searchsorted side='left'). r20 and regime A use the previous close. dte uses the scanner's contract expiry, which is known at the signal. Setting c, the one chosen, uses only s_opus, s_fable_op and their product.

No overlap between training and test rows. Models are fitted on real 12 May-31 Aug only. Design rows are scored only with OOF p. Real 2nd half and unseen are scored by the refit model. Known shares the design dates and is correctly labelled as contaminated.

Mild in-sample element in the DESIGN figures only. Platt is fitted per side on the same OOF rows it then scores, so the sign per side (the short side is reversed, a=+0.275) and the scaling between sides are set with design labels. spec.name: Equal option-risk lot sizing at the baseline's total premium outlay (delta-times-stop loss per contract with a 20 % pad; reduce size rather than tighten the stop)
spec.hypothesis: Futures sizing equalises the FUTURES loss at the stop. The bought option's loss at that same stop is (delta*R - 0.5*gamma*R^2 + decay + costs), which varies widely: small where the stop is wide relative to the option's implied move (strong convexity cushion), large where it is tight (all decay and spread). Sizing each trade so that the modelled option loss at the stop is equal moves lots toward trades whose option asymmetry is best. Holding total premium outlay at the baseline's level makes this a reallocation rather than added leverage. The brief names lot count for a bought option as an open lever.
spec.exact_rules: Picks unchanged: t = H.pick(df, S, 75, 6), S = 's_fable_op' (exit T3) or 's_opus_v3' (exit T1). Per picked row: call = (o_kind=='CE'); sgn = +1 if call else -1; F0 = o_F0; K = F0 (ATM, as the scanner); T0 = H._years(o_entry_ts, o_expiry); s = o_iv; p0 = H._b76(F0, K, T0, s, call); pS = H._b76(F0 - sgn*o_risk_abs, K, T0, s, call), the premium with the underlying at the futures stop and no decay (the pad covers decay, IV and spread). lot: column 'lot' on unseen/known. On real, the known set's 'lot' for the same symbol on the nearest date <= day (else the nearest after); if o_qty % lot != 0, lot = o_qty (treated as one lot). fut_lots = o_qty/lot. Per-lot option loss at the stop: Ll = 1.2*(p0 - pS)*lot + H.opt_costs(p0, pS, lot). New lots L = clip(floor(B/Ll), 1, cap*fut_lots). pnl = H.option_net(t, pol, qty=L*lot); outlay = H.option_net(t, pol, qty=L*lot, detail=True).outlay. The trade function returns t with this 'pnl' column (harness run() keeps a supplied pnl); futures reference = net_<pol> * L/fut_lots. Capital-neutral budget B_eq: bisection over Rs 1,000-60,000 (tolerance Rs 10) on the DESIGN-window picks of that setting only, so that sum(new outlay) = sum(p0*o_qty) for the same picks. B_eq is then frozen and applied unchanged to all sets.
spec.fixed_params: Loss per contract = move to the stop through the option's price sensitivity (Black-76 repricing in place of delta*distance), padded 20 % (Tradefundrr). Lots = planned risk / backstop loss per contract (Tradefundrr; EPAT floor-to-whole-lots). The underlying (futures) stop and exit are kept; only size changes (Quantsapp: reduce size rather than tighten the stop). Rs 15,000 risk budget, ATM monthly contract and roll rule as the scanner.
spec.grid: (a) Fable-OP>=75, T3, cap 2x futures lots, B = B_eq. (b) Fable-OP>=75, T3, cap 3x, B = B_eq. (c) Opus v3>=75, T1, cap 3x, B = B_eq (its own B_eq). (d) Fable-OP>=75, T3, cap 3x, B = Rs 15,000 of modelled option loss at the stop: the brief's literal 'same Rs 15,000 risk', with more capital. Choose on the design window by option net, but only among settings whose design option worst day and max DD are no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline (else highest net, flagged). Setting (d) is always reported separately as a leverage variant.
spec.exit_policy: Unchanged: T3 for the Fable-OP settings, T1 for the Opus v3 setting; the option is sold the minute after the futures leg exits.
spec.selection: The baseline live rule unchanged (first 6 per day with score >= 75 in time order); only the option quantity per trade changes.

Because lot count changes, report separately: premium outlay per trade (mean, median, max), the largest single-day total outlay, total outlay vs the baseline, option worst day and max DD, plus futures net at the new lots for reference.

spec.name: Prior-day range compression bonus (NR4 / NR7 / triangle) and no same-direction trade after a prior trend day (Zarattini et al. Table 5; Crabel; Unofficed NR7 F&O test)
spec.hypothesis: A breakout out of a compressed prior-day range is a volatility-expansion event with room left to its typical daily range. That suits a bought option, which needs the move to happen. After a full trend day in the same direction, next-day momentum fails. Zarattini et al. report next-day intraday-momentum P&L of 22 bps (t 5.1) after NR4, 16 bps after NR7 and 14 bps after triangles, against 12 bps unconditional, and -2 bps (Sharpe -0.3) after trend days. No current score or harness feature uses prior-day range patterns.
spec.exact_rules: Cash daily candles from H.minute_data() (from Jan 2024), using only candles dated before d. Short sessions (fewer than 300 Nifty minute bars, e.g. Muhurat) are dropped before computing patterns. Index the last k full sessions before d as d-1, d-2, ...; rng = High - Low. NR4: rng[d-1] == min(rng[d-4..d-1]). NR7: rng[d-1] == min(rng[d-7..d-1]). Triangle: High[d-1] < min(High[d-2], High[d-3]) and Low[d-1] > max(Low[d-2], Low[d-3]). compressed = NR4 or NR7 or Triangle. Trend day in trade direction: for a LONG, Open[d-1] <= Low[d-1] + 0.15*rng[d-1] and Close[d-1] >= Low[d-1] + 0.85*rng[d-1] and rng[d-1] > mean(rng over the 14 sessions before d-1); for a SHORT, Open[d-1] >= Low[d-1] + 0.85*rng[d-1] and Close[d-1] <= Low[d-1] + 0.15*rng[d-1] and the same range condition. Fewer than 16 prior sessions: no flags. Specs (adjust or mask before pick): S1 score = s_fable_op + 10*compressed, pick(...,75,6), T3. S2 score = s_fable_op, NaN where trend_day_same_dir, pick(...,75,6), T3. S3 = S1 and S2 together, T3. S4 = S3 applied to s_opus_v3, T1. Uses the harness opt_<pol>/net_<pol> columns.
spec.fixed_params: NR4 (4 days), NR7 (7 days), triangle with a 2-day lookback, trend day at the 15/85 % range positions with range above the 14-day mean (all from the paper's Table 5 definitions). The bonus of +10 points is the size the candidate declared, set so that 65-74 signals can enter on compressed days; it is not tuned.
spec.grid: S1: +10 bonus when compressed (Fable-OP, T3). S2: drop signals after a same-direction trend day (Fable-OP, T3). S3: S1 + S2 (Fable-OP, T3). S4: S1 + S2 on Opus v3 (T1). Choose on real 12 May-31 Aug by option net, subject to design worst day and max DD no worse than 1.25x the better design baseline (else highest net, flagged).
spec.exit_policy: Unchanged harness policies: T3 for the Fable-OP settings, T1 for the Opus v3 setting.
spec.selection: Live rule: per day in time order (ties: higher adjusted score, then symbol), the first 6 rows whose adjusted or masked score >= 75.
spec.compare_on: All three sets from the harness columns (pre-open flags on existing rows); real is judged on the real futures path. The bar is on unseen and real 2nd half; known is reported as a cross-check. Report flag frequencies per set, option net, worst day, max DD, futures net and Switch-1.

result.deviations: None material. (1) The short-session rule needs Nifty minute bars, which exist only from 15 Oct 2025. result.summary:
The candidate does not clear the bar. The design window picked S2: Fable-OP exit T3, skipping any signal that follows a same-direction trend day.

Option net:
- **Unseen:** +2,15,436. That beats Opus v3 (+84,362) and Fable-OP (+2,02,948) but not Switch-1 (+2,67,606).
- **Real 2nd half:** +1,94,376. That beats Opus v3 (+1,84,693) but falls Rs 3,312 short of Fable-OP (+1,97,688), and short of Switch-1 (+2,43,042).
- **Risk:** passes on unseen (worst day -15,161, max DD -42,207). Fails on real 2nd half: worst day -26,335 against a limit of -18,788. That is the same day as Fable-OP's own worst day, so the failure comes from the base model; max DD there is -28,927, within its limit.

Whole sets, option net / futures net:
- Real: +5,78,186 / +7,97,711, against Fable-OP +5,45,031 / +7,02,290.
- Unseen: +2,15,436 / +1,24,990, against Fable-OP +2,02,948 / +78,849.
- Known (cross-check): +2,14,185 / +1,18,304, against Opus v3 +1,99,051 and Fable-OP +1,83,848.

How often the flags fire:
- Compressed prior day (NR4 or NR7 or triangle): 24-27% of all rows and 18-26% of Fable-OP >= 75 rows. NR4 is 24-26% of rows, NR7 13-17%, triangle only 1.7-2.6%.
- Same-direction trend day: 9-10% of rows and 6-9% of Fable-OP >= 75 rows.

What each part did:
- **Trend-day mask:** Fable-OP baseline picks that followed a same-direction trend day lost money on option net in all three sets: real n=19, -22,307; unseen n=19, -14,873; known n=14, -11,159. This matches the paper's sign, but the counts are small.
- **Compression bonus:** it does not hold up out of sample. S1 lets in about 100-111 trades scoring 65-74.9 on compressed days. Those trades made +71,201 option net on real but lost on unseen (-15,025 option, -1,52,708 futures) and on known (-32,307 option, -1,58,971 futures). Fable-OP's own picks earned no more per trade on compressed days than on other days (real +1,840 vs +2,448; unseen +887 vs +870; known -2 vs +1,016).
result.caveats:
1. **Thin margins.** S2's lead over Fable-OP on unseen is Rs 12,488 (about 6%), inside the stated +-10% error of the option model. Its shortfall on real 2nd half is Rs 3,312. The mask removes only 14-19 baseline trades per set, so the effect rests on very few trades.
2. **S3 near-miss.** S3 (bonus and mask) failed the design worst-day limit by Rs 84 (-23,662 against -23,578), so it was not chosen. It does better on real 2nd half (+2,81,793, ahead of both baselines and Switch-1). On unseen it makes +1,99,061, below Fable-OP's +2,02,948, with max DD -88,864 against a limit of -61,094. So S3 would also have failed the bar, on unseen net and on risk.
3. **S1 and S4 elsewhere.** S1 loses to Fable-OP on unseen (+1,90,791) and on known (+1,64,640), with deeper drawdowns (unseen max DD -87,255). S4 loses to its base model Opus v3 on real (+3,65,976 against +4,23,981) and on unseen (+51,409 against +84,362).
4. **Known overlaps real.** The `known` set covers the same dates as `real` (cash stand-in), so it is only a cross-check.
5. **Modelled options.** All option figures are modelled (Black-76 with fitted IV and decay, no skew).
6. **Half rows.** In the `rows` list, rows labelled *_h1 or *_h2 show 0 for the other half's net; it does not apply there.
7. **No extra variants.** No exploratory variants beyond the four pre-registered settings were run.

leakage_or_bugs: No look-ahead found. Flags use only cash daily candles dated strictly before d (searchsorted 'left' on date strings, plus an assert that prev_day < day). The trend-day range mean is taken over d-15..d-2. No net_*/r_*/status_* columns feed adj(); outcome columns appear only in the diagnostic prints. The design choice reads only the real h1 stats.

Stale-candle check, done independently: for every row in all three sets (14,129 rows), the symbol's last daily candle before d is the calendar's previous session (0 mismatches). No signal's d-1 points to an older candle because of a data gap.

Option pricing is honest: opt_T1 and opt_T3 in sets_opt.pkl equal a fresh H.option_net(D[s], pol) to 0.000000 Rs on all three sets. The candidate is priced through H.run's opt_<pol> columns, with no outcome-dependent shortcut.
Live constraints are kept: at most 6 trades a day (asserted), lots unchanged (o_qty, Rs 15,000 futures-risk sizing), harness costs, unchanged T3 exit for S2.
Minor rounding only: the summary says the real h2 worst-day limit is -18,788; the log prints -18,787 (1.25 x -15,030 = -18,787.5).

verdict.overfit_concerns: Few choices were made: 4 pre-registered settings with fixed literature parameters, picked on the real 12 May-31 Aug window under the stated risk limits. S3 missed the worst-day limit by only Rs 84 and was correctly excluded. The chosen S2 is almost a subset of Fable-OP: it drops the 14-19 baseline picks that followed a same-direction trend day and adds 1-3. The edge is tiny next to the noise. On unseen, the S2 minus Fable-OP per-day difference totals +12,489 over 127 days, but only 17 days differ. A day bootstrap (20,000 reps) gives a 90% CI of [-32,596, +55,863] and P(diff <= 0) = 0.315. Real 2nd half: -3,312 (4 days differ, P = 0.50); one removed trade, PATANJALI on 21 Sep (+24,972), outweighs the five removed losers. Real 1st half (design): +36,467, P(diff <= 0) = 0.097. Known: +30,337, P = 0.20. The removed trend-same picks lose on average in every set (real n=19, -1,174 per trade; unseen n=19, -783; known n=14, -797), which matches the paper's sign. Pooled over unseen and real, though, n=38 with a mean of -978 and t = -0.85: not significant. Halves: S2 beats Fable-OP in both unseen halves (+5,476 / +7,013) and both known halves (+24,952 / +5,385), but loses in real h2 (-3,312). It beats Opus v3 in every half shown. The compression bonus (S1, S3, S4) clearly overfits the design window. Its added 65-74.9 trades earn +71k option net on real but lose on unseen (-15k option, -153k futures) and on known (-32k option, -159k futures).

It computes its own flags with pandas rolling windows and per-symbol searchsorted, finds short sessions from Nifty minute counts (2025-10-21: 60 bars, 2026-11-08: 70 bars), and uses its own pick (stable sort by day, time, -score, symbol; cumcount < 6) and its own stats (per-day sums reindexed to the set's days, max DD floored at 0). Every trade is re-priced with H.option_net. All 6 models (V3, FOP, S1-S4) on all 3 sets and both halves match the tester exactly. S2: real n 216, +578,186 (worst day -26,335, max DD -28,927). Real h1: +383,810 (-23,143 / -23,143). Real h2: n 67, +194,376 (-26,335 / -28,927). Unseen: n 214, +215,436 (-15,161 / -42,207); unseen halves +89,319 / +126,117. Known: +214,185. verdict.notes: The tester's numbers and conclusion are correct: the candidate (S2, Fable-OP T3 with signals after a same-direction prior trend day masked) does not meet the BRIEF.md option-net bar. It beats both baselines on unseen (+215,436 vs +202,948 / +84,362). On real 2nd half it falls Rs 3,312 short of Fable-OP (+194,376 vs +197,688), and its real-h2 worst day of -26,335 (inherited from Fable-OP's own worst day) breaks the -18,788 limit set by Opus v3's -15,030. It also trails Switch-1 on both test sets (+267,606 unseen, +243,042 real h2). Even the unseen lead is within noise (bootstrap P(diff <= 0) about 0.32) and within the stated +-10% error of the option model. The trend-day mask has the right sign in every set but rests on roughly 14-19 trades per set, so at most it is a weak hint for later work, not a proven improvement.
